                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                🔍 Module 6 Review Questions

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Pick an answer — the explanation opens right away.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Q1Companion Care Clinic's transferred balance

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Companion Care Clinic, customer 1310, currently shows a BALANCE of 0.00. KimTay's bookkeeper learns the account was migrated from an older system and that nobody can confirm what the clinic actually owes. What should be stored in BALANCE, and why?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • ✘a. Zero is a claim that the clinic owes nothing. Having no invoice yet is not the same as having a verified balance of zero.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • ✘b. BALANCE is a numeric column, so text will be rejected or coerced; and inventing a code word is what null exists to replace.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • ✔c. Correct: null means the value is unknown or does not apply, which is exactly the state of this balance.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • ✘d. An empty string is a text value of zero length, not an absence, and it does not belong in a DECIMAL column at all.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Remember: Null records that a fact is unknown; zero records that the fact is known and happens to be nothing.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Q2The average that moved on its own

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                A clerk at KimTay runs AVG(BALANCE) over the four customers and gets 2383.3125. She then sets Companion Care Clinic's balance to null and runs the identical query, which now returns 3177.75. SUM(BALANCE) reads 9533.25 both times. What happened?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • ✔a. Correct: aggregate functions ignore nulls. The row held 0.00, so the total was unchanged, but the divisor dropped from four to three.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • ✘b. Nulling a column never moves its old value anywhere. The value is gone.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • ✘c. Null has no magnitude at all, so it is neither the highest nor the lowest value; it is excluded from the calculation.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • ✘d. UPDATE changes a column in a row; it never deletes the row. COUNT(*) still returns 4.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Remember: COUNT(column), SUM, and AVG all skip nulls, so nulling one value changes the divisor as well as the total.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Q3The search that found nothing

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                After nulling several balances, a KimTay analyst writes SELECT CUSTOMER_NAME FROM CUSTOMER WHERE BALANCE = NULL; and gets back no rows at all, even though she can see nulls in the table. What is wrong?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • ✘a. Nulls set with the bare keyword are not text. If they had been stored as the quoted string 'NULL' they would be findable by equality, which is one reason quoting the keyword is a bug rather than a shortcut.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • ✘b. ORDER BY only sorts the rows a WHERE clause has already kept; it has no effect on which rows match.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • ✘c. That operator exists in some engines but is not the lesson here, and equality fails on null in every column type, not only numeric ones.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • ✔d. Correct: comparing anything to null yields unknown, and a WHERE clause keeps only rows where the condition is definitely true.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Remember: IS NULL and IS NOT NULL are the only tests that work on nulls; = and <> silently match nothing.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Q4The refused update at StayWell

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                A StayWell staff member tries UPDATE STUDENT SET LAST_NAME = NULL WHERE STUDENT_ID = 'S002'; and the engine rejects it with a NOT NULL constraint failure. The row is unchanged. What is the correct reading of this?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • ✘a. Constraint failures have nothing to do with disk space; the engine refused on a rule, not a resource.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • ✔b. Correct: STUDENT.LAST_NAME is declared NOT NULL in the table definition, and the engine enforces it on every write.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • ✘c. This is backwards. Primary key columns are the ones that must never be null; other columns are the ones that usually may be.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • ✘d. A rejected statement changed nothing, so there is nothing to commit. COMMIT never overrides a constraint.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Remember: A NOT NULL rejection is the table design working; the fix is to question the row, not to drop the constraint.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Q5New email column at KimTay

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                KimTay runs ALTER TABLE CUSTOMER ADD COLUMN EMAIL VARCHAR(40); on a table that already holds four customers. Immediately afterward, what does SELECT CUSTOMER_NUM, EMAIL FROM CUSTOMER; return?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • ✔a. Correct: ADD COLUMN appends the column and puts a null in it for every row that already exists.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • ✘b. Adding a column changes every row at once. No row is left behind or hidden.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • ✘c. CHAR and VARCHAR columns hold nulls perfectly well unless declared NOT NULL, and the engine does not substitute an empty string.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • ✘d. Adding a nullable column to a populated table is routine. Only a NOT NULL column without a DEFAULT is refused.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Remember: A newly added column is null on every existing row, which is why nulls and ALTER TABLE are taught together.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Q6Widening a description at KimTay

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Product names have outgrown ITEM.DESCRIPTION, which is VARCHAR(30). The team needs VARCHAR(40). They are working in the SQLite engine behind this page. What has to happen?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • ✘a. MODIFY is MySQL and Oracle syntax, and SQLite rejects it with 'near "MODIFY": syntax error'. There is no portable spelling for retyping a column.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • ✘b. Deleting the rows does not make the column wider, and retyping data by hand invites errors the copy pattern avoids entirely.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • ✔c. Correct: create, copy, drop, rename is the portable pattern and the only option in SQLite, which cannot retype a column.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • ✘d. Two columns holding the same fact is a design problem, and every query and report would then need to handle both.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Remember: When an engine will not change a column in place, rebuild the table under a new name and rename it into position.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Q7The rebuild that lost its index

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                A StayWell administrator rebuilds ROOM with the copy-and-rename pattern. All five rows arrive safely and every query returns correct results, but a nightly report that used to finish in seconds now takes minutes. What was most likely lost?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • ✘a. The primary key is part of the CREATE TABLE you write in step one, so it is recreated as long as you include it, and a two-column PRIMARY KEY clause is perfectly ordinary.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • ✔b. Correct: DROP TABLE removes the table's indexes with it, and the copy pattern carries rows, not the objects built on the table.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • ✘c. The results are correct, so the values arrived intact. Nulled capacities would have produced wrong numbers, not slow ones.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • ✘d. Same problem: a null rent would change the report's output, and the scenario says the output is right and only the speed changed.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Remember: The copy pattern moves rows only; plan to recreate indexes, views, and triggers in the same script.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Q8Two ways to clear the archive

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                KimTay keeps a scratch table, ITEM_ARCHIVE, that a Monday-morning script refills with INSERT statements. The script assumes the table is already there and never creates it. On Friday the team wants the table emptied, but wants Monday's script to keep working without any change. Which statement fits?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • ✘a. This erases the structure too, so Monday's insert-only script would fail with 'no such table' instead of filling the table.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • ✘b. Dropping a column removes one column from every row; it does not remove rows, and where the column is a key or is indexed the engine refuses outright.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • ✘c. IF EXISTS only prevents an error when the table is absent. The statement still destroys the structure along with the rows, so Monday's script still fails.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • ✔d. Correct: DELETE empties the table and leaves its structure standing, so an insert-only script keeps working unchanged.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Remember: DELETE empties a table; DROP TABLE erases it, structure and all.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Q9Retiring the invoice tables at KimTay

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                KimTay is removing INVOICE_LINE, INVOICE, and ITEM from a MySQL database that enforces foreign keys. INVOICE_LINE references both INVOICE and ITEM, and neither INVOICE nor ITEM references the other. In what order must the drops run?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • ✘a. Row counts are irrelevant. Dropping ITEM first is refused, because INVOICE_LINE still holds rows referencing it.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • ✘b. This drops a parent before its child as well, so the first statement fails on the constraint from INVOICE_LINE.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • ✔c. Correct: the table holding the foreign keys goes first, after which nothing references INVOICE or ITEM and the two remaining drops are independent of each other.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • ✘d. No engine reorders your statements. Each DROP is evaluated on its own and fails if a constraint still points at the table.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Remember: Drop children before parents; tables that do not reference each other may go in any order.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Q10The orphaned lines on invoice 50712

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Someone drops ITEM on a KimTay database that is not enforcing foreign keys. All six INVOICE_LINE rows are still present. A report then runs SELECT L.INVOICE_NUM, I.DESCRIPTION FROM INVOICE_LINE L INNER JOIN ITEM I ON L.ITEM_ID = I.ITEM_ID; What happens, and what is the underlying problem?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • ✔a. Correct: the engine cannot resolve the table name at all, so the statement fails outright, and the invoice lines are orphaned.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • ✘b. That is what an outer join to an existing but unmatched table would do. A missing table is a different failure entirely.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • ✘c. A missing table is caught when the statement is prepared, not an empty result set. The query never runs.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • ✘d. INVOICE_LINE stores ITEM_ID, NUM_ORDERED, and QUOTED_PRICE only. The description lived exclusively in ITEM.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Remember: Dropping a parent table does not clean up the rows that referenced it; it leaves orphans and breaks every query that joined to it.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Exercise 6: order the drops correctly

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                KimTay is retiring the invoicing side of the database and keeping only CUSTOMER and REP. Write the DROP TABLE statements in an order that would not violate a single foreign key on an engine that enforces them, and confirm which tables are left. Putting INVOICE_LINE anywhere but first would have failed on MySQL or Oracle, because it would still have held rows naming invoices or items that no longer existed, and IF EXISTS would not have rescued you: it suppresses a missing table, not a constraint violation. The sandbox does not enforce that check, which is exactly why the order is worth getting right by habit rather than by error message.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Before you do any of this for real

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Every statement in these six exercises is permanent on a live database. On the job, the sequence is: write the SELECT that shows you the rows you are about to affect, take a backup or open a transaction, run one statement, check the result, and only then run the next. The sandbox forgives you. Production does not.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                7-1 Creating and Using Views

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                A view is a stored query. You hand the database a SELECT statement, give it a name, and from that point on the name can be used almost anywhere a table name is allowed. Nothing is copied. No second set of rows is written anywhere. The rows you see through a view still live in the tables underneath it.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Start with the data: the first view reads from ITEM. This is the complete base table before the HABITAT view filters its rows and columns.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Base table: ITEM — the rows available to the first view
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                ITEM_IDDESCRIPTIONCATEGORYON_HANDPRICEREORDER_LEVEL
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                AV07Aviary Starter CageHabitat1564.995
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                CF21Grain-Free Dry Food 30lbFood4842.5015
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                DG04Nylon Dog Leash 6ftAccessory12011.9925
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                FT88Fish Tank Filter KitHabitat3027.7510
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                GR15Small Animal Grooming KitGrooming2215.258
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                📖
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Three words you need

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                The base tables are the real tables the data lives in, such as ITEM and CUSTOMER. The defining query is the SELECT statement you stored. The view is the name you gave that query. A view has no rows of its own.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                The syntax is short. You write CREATE VIEW, the name, the word AS, and then any SELECT statement you already know how to write.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                -- CREATE VIEW: gives a name to a query. Nothing is copied and no rows are stored -
--   the view is the SELECT statement below, saved under a name you can use as
--   though it were a table.
CREATE VIEW view_name AS

-- SELECT: the columns the view will appear to have. Whatever this list returns is
--   the shape of the view.
SELECT column_list

-- FROM: the real table or tables the data actually lives in. These are called the
--   base tables, and they are where every value really comes from.
FROM   table_list

-- WHERE: the rows the view will appear to contain. Anyone querying the view sees
--   only these, which is what makes a view useful for hiding rows as well as
--   columns. The whole statement is stored; it is re-run every time the view is
--   used, so the view is always current.
WHERE  condition;

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                KimTay's ITEM table mixes four categories together. A buyer who only handles habitat products has to remember to add WHERE CATEGORY = 'Habitat' to every single query, and has to get it right every single time. A view removes that burden. Run this.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                SQL Sandbox · SQLite engine
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                In this databaseclick a table to see its rows
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                The view returns AV07 and FT88. Notice the second query in the solution: once HABITAT exists you can put a WHERE clause on it exactly as if it were a table. That second query returns FT88 alone.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Two things just happened that are worth naming. The view narrowed the rows, keeping only the habitat items, and it narrowed the columns, dropping CATEGORY and REORDER_LEVEL from sight. Views can do either or both.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Simplification

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                A four-table join with a dozen conditions is hard to type and easy to get subtly wrong. Store it once as a view and every report after that is a plain SELECT from a single name. One query to review, one query to fix when the rules change.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Showing only part of a table

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                CUSTOMER holds credit limits. Counter staff need names and balances but have no business seeing credit limits. Build a view with only the permitted columns and give access to the view instead of the table. What is not in the view cannot be read through it.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                A view is always current

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                This is the part that surprises people. The defining query is not run when you create the view. It is run every time you use the view. That means a view can never go stale. If somebody adds a habitat item to ITEM at four in the afternoon, the next person to select from HABITAT sees it. Watch it happen.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                SQL Sandbox · SQLite engine
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                In this databaseclick a table to see its rows
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Two items were inserted but the second SELECT from the view grows by only one row, from two to three. TR55 is a habitat item so it qualifies; CH12 is an accessory so the defining query's WHERE clause leaves it out. The view was never touched by the INSERT statements. It simply asked the question again.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                📝
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                About the numbers you see

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                This engine stores DECIMAL values as ordinary numbers, so a stored 42.50 is displayed as 42.5, 85.00 as 85, and 7500.00 as 7500. The value is right; the trailing zeros are a formatting choice, not a change in the data.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Naming the view's columns

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                By default a view's columns inherit the names in the SELECT list. You can rename them by listing new names in parentheses after the view name. Do this when the base column names are cryptic, when two joined tables both contribute a column of the same name, or when a column is computed and would otherwise have no sensible name at all.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                SQL Sandbox · SQLite engine
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                In this databaseclick a table to see its rows
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                The column headings come back as ID, ITEM_NAME, UNITS and UNIT_PRICE, with FT88 first and AV07 second. From here on, ORDER BY PRICE against this view fails with no such column: PRICE: outside the view those columns no longer answer to their old names.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                A view over a join

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                This is where views start earning real money. Pulling an invoice line together with its item description and its customer name takes a four-table join. Nobody wants to retype that for the sales report, the reorder report and the collections report. Write it once.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                SQL Sandbox · SQLite engine
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                In this databaseclick a table to see its rows
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                The first query returns four lines over fifty dollars: 127.5, 85, 64.99 and 55.5. The solution adds a second, completely different question answered from the same view, with no join written a second time. That reuse is the whole point.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Notice LINE_TOTAL. A computed column needs a name, and the alias you give it in the defining query becomes a column of the view. Once the view exists, LINE_TOTAL can be used in a WHERE clause, in ORDER BY, and in SUM, as though the number were stored.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                A view over grouped data

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                A view can also summarize. Group the invoice lines by invoice number, total them, and store that as a view. Everyone downstream now has invoice totals without knowing that INVOICE_LINE exists.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                SQL Sandbox · SQLite engine
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                In this databaseclick a table to see its rows
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Invoice 50710 comes to 151.48, invoice 50711 to 100.25 and invoice 50712 to 120.49. The second query filters on TOTAL, which in a direct query would have needed HAVING. Through the view it is an ordinary column, so a plain WHERE works. Remember the shape of this view: section 7-2c explains why a view built this way can never be written to.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                📝
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                A view is not a cache

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Because the defining query runs on every use, a view built on an expensive join costs you that join every time. It buys clarity, not speed. Oracle offers materialized views, which really do store results and must be refreshed. MySQL and this engine have no such feature, so every view you write here is recomputed on demand.

Replace each ____ so the view holds every item priced above twenty dollars, then select from it in descending price order. Press Run, and check yourself against the solution.
