                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Summary What You Learned in Module 7

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Module 7 was about the work that surrounds the data rather than the data itself: what other people are allowed to see, how quickly the engine can find a row, what the database knows about its own shape, and which rules it will refuse to break. None of it changes a single value in CUSTOMER. All of it decides whether the values in CUSTOMER can be trusted and whether the database can be maintained by somebody who did not build it.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Views

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        A view is a query stored under a name and used as if it were a table. It holds no data of its own; the defining query runs every time the view is used, which is why a view is never out of date. Views give a user a row-and-column subset of a table, simplify a join that people would otherwise rewrite by hand, and hide columns nobody outside the office should see. On this page you can create a view and select from it. You cannot update through one, because SQLite answers cannot modify V because it is a view. MySQL permits it for simple views.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Security

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        GRANT gives a named user a specific privilege on a specific object, and REVOKE takes it back. The privilege is narrow on purpose: SELECT on one table, or UPDATE on one column, rather than the run of the database. Combine it with a view and you can let somebody read three columns of CUSTOMER and nothing else. Neither statement exists in SQLite at all, so both are MySQL and Oracle material, and both are examinable.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Indexes

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        An index is a structure the DBMS keeps so it can find rows by a column value without reading every row. CREATE INDEX builds one, DROP INDEX removes it, and the optimizer decides when to use it; you never name an index in a SELECT. Indexes cost space and slow down every INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE that has to maintain them, which is why you index the columns you search and join on rather than all of them. A unique index also refuses duplicates, the same work a UNIQUE constraint does.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        The system catalog

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        The catalog is the database describing itself. MySQL exposes it as INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES, .COLUMNS, .VIEWS, and .STATISTICS; SQLite exposes sqlite_master and pragma_table_info; Oracle uses USER_TABLES and USER_TAB_COLUMNS. The DBMS updates it as part of every CREATE, ALTER, and DROP, so it is never stale. Read it freely and never write to it.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Integrity constraints

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        PRIMARY KEY, UNIQUE, NOT NULL, CHECK, and FOREIGN KEY are rules the DBMS enforces on every statement, from every program, forever. Declare them in CREATE TABLE. On SQLite, turn foreign keys on with PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON per connection; MySQL and Oracle enforce them always. And remember the one SQLite lets through: a primary key column is not automatically NOT NULL, so write it.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        SQL Sandbox · SQLite engine
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        In this databaseclick a table to see its rows
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        The starter counts the ten entries the shipped database already has. Build one view and one index, then ask the catalog what you built. Both DROP ... IF EXISTS lines are there so you can press Run twice.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Three of this module's five themes in one short script. The view and the index both show up in the catalog the moment they exist, and the view returns Whiskers and Wags Boutique, Access Pet Center, and Downtown Aquarium and Pets, the three customers with a balance over 1000. Companion Care Clinic sits at 0.00 and stays out of it.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        💡
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        The habit to carry forward

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        When you can put a rule in the database instead of in a program, put it in the database. Applications get rewritten, replaced, and bypassed; the table outlives all of them. The same instinct applies to the catalog: before you change a column, ask the database what depends on it rather than trusting your memory of the schema.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • I can declare all five integrity constraints in a CREATE TABLE
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • I can demonstrate referential integrity being enforced and explain what it prevented

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Defining queryThe SELECT a view is built from. The DBMS runs it again every time the view is used.Views, why a view is never stale
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Row-and-column subset viewA view that exposes some rows and some columns of one table and hides the rest.Views, showing a clerk part of a table
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Updatable viewA view you can change data through. MySQL allows it for simple views; SQLite refuses with cannot modify V because it is a view.Views, the engine note
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        GRANT / REVOKEStatements that give a user a privilege on an object and take it away again. MySQL and Oracle only.Security, granting SELECT on one table
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        PrivilegeOne specific right, such as SELECT on CUSTOMER, held by one specific user.Security, the narrow grant
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        IndexA structure the DBMS keeps so it can find rows by a column value without reading them all.Indexes, speeding up a search

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Module 7 key terms, part two: the catalog and the rules
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        TermWhat it meansWhere you used it
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        System catalogThe tables in which the DBMS records what tables, columns, views, and indexes exist. Also called the data dictionary.7-6, the whole section
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        INFORMATION_SCHEMAMySQL's catalog, queried through TABLES, COLUMNS, VIEWS, and STATISTICS. Absent in SQLite.7-6, the engine comparison
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        sqlite_masterSQLite's single catalog table: one row per table, view, index, and trigger, with the sql that created it.7-6, listing the KimTay tables
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        pragma_table_infoA SQLite function returning one row per column of a named table, with type, notnull, and pk.7-6, the columns of REP
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Integrity constraintA rule stored with the table and enforced by the DBMS on every insert, update, and delete.7-7, the SUPPLIER table
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        PRIMARY KEYThe identifier for a row: unique, and not null on every engine except SQLite.7-7, and the null-key demonstration
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        UNIQUENo duplicates allowed, nulls still permitted. Weaker than a primary key.7-7, one email per supplier
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        CHECKA condition every row must satisfy, best given a name so the error says which rule failed.7-7, LEAD_DAYS_POSITIVE
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        FOREIGN KEYA column whose value must already exist in a parent table's key.7-7, INVOICE_LINE to ITEM
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Referential integrityThe state in which every foreign key value points at a row that exists.7-7, the refused insert and the refused delete
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        PRAGMA foreign_keysThe SQLite switch that turns foreign key enforcement on for the current connection. Off by default.7-7, the two sandboxes side by side
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Orphan rowA row whose foreign key points at a parent that is not there.7-7, the invoice line for ZZ99
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        📖
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Data dictionary

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Another name for the system catalog. Textbooks, Oracle documentation, and job postings all use it. If an interviewer asks how you would find every table containing a CUSTOMER_NUM, the answer they are listening for is the data dictionary, whatever the engine calls it.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        One short check that ties the two halves of the module together. A constraint is not stored somewhere separate from the table; it is part of the table's definition, which means it is part of the catalog entry. Read the entry and you read the rules.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        SQL Sandbox · SQLite engine
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        In this databaseclick a table to see its rows
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        The sql column holds the text of the CREATE TABLE. Search that text for the words you care about.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        The starter prints the whole definition of INVOICE_LINE, two-column primary key and both foreign keys included. The solution turns the same idea into an audit: CUSTOMER, INVOICE, and INVOICE_LINE declare a foreign key, and ITEM and REP do not, because nothing in this database sits above them.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Review Module 7 Review

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  The ten questions below are cumulative. Most of them come from 7-6 and 7-7, but several reach back to the joins, aggregates, nulls, subqueries, and ALTER TABLE work you have been doing since Module 4, because that is how this material arrives in practice. A constraint gets added and a query that used to work has to be checked. A table gets rebuilt and the catalog is the only place to confirm it. Read each scenario, decide before you look at the options, and read every note afterward, including the ones for answers you did not choose.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  💡
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  How to use the notes

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Each wrong option has a note naming the specific mistake it stands for. Those mistakes are the ones that cost people real data, so the note is worth more than the checkmark. If a note describes something you would have done, go back to the section it came from before moving on.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Warm up in the sandbox first. This one puts a constrained table next to the shipped data, joins across, and then asks the catalog what it created, which is 7-6 and 7-7 in a single short script.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  SQL Sandbox · SQLite engine
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  In this databaseclick a table to see its rows
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Build the table with a named CHECK and a foreign key, add two requests, join to ITEM for the descriptions, then count what the table put in the catalog. Keep the DROP TABLE IF EXISTS so you can run it twice.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  The join returns the grain-free dry food and the small animal grooming kit with their quantities. CATALOG_ENTRIES comes back as 2: the table itself and the index SQLite built to enforce REQUEST_ID. The CHECK and the FOREIGN KEY did not add entries of their own, because they live inside the stored text of the CREATE TABLE, which the starter query showed you for ITEM.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • I can read a database I did not build using only the catalog
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • I can name the catalog objects in MySQL, SQLite, and Oracle
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • I can declare every constraint type and predict the error each one raises
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • I can show referential integrity being enforced in both directions
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • I can explain why a view stays current and an index costs something
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • I can decide whether a rule belongs in the application or in the table

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  🔍 🔍 Module 7 Review Questions

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Pick an answer — the explanation opens right away.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Q1Two questions about Access Pet Center

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  A KimTay analyst has two questions: what balance is stored for Access Pet Center, and what type and size the BALANCE column was declared with. Which statement about answering them is correct?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • ✘a. The catalog records structure only; it has never held a single customer balance.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • ✘b. A SELECT returns values, and the column headings, but not the declared type or size.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • ✔c. Correct: values live in the table, definitions live in the catalog, and each answers its own kind of question.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • ✘d. Reading your own tables and your own catalog entries needs no special privilege at all.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Remember: Values come from the table; types, sizes, and null settings come from the catalog.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Q2The invoice line that disappears from a join

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  With foreign key enforcement off, someone inserts an INVOICE_LINE row for item ZZ99. SELECT COUNT(*) FROM INVOICE_LINE returns 7, but the same count over INVOICE_LINE inner joined to ITEM returns 6. What has happened?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • ✔a. Correct: an inner join keeps only matched rows, so a row pointing at nothing silently vanishes.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • ✘b. The join is written correctly; the mismatch is a data problem the join is exposing, not causing.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • ✘c. COUNT(*) counts rows and ignores nulls in columns entirely; the join lost the row, not the count.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • ✘d. Nothing was rolled back: with enforcement off the row was accepted and is in the table.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Remember: Orphan rows do not announce themselves; they show up as counts that quietly refuse to agree.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Q3Reading the catalog entry for INVOICE_LINE

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Running SELECT name, type, "notnull", pk FROM pragma_table_info('INVOICE_LINE') returns pk values of 1 for INVOICE_NUM, 2 for ITEM_ID, and 0 for the other two columns. What does that describe?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • ✘a. A table has exactly one primary key; there is no ranking of several keys.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • ✘b. pk numbers key position, not key kind; foreign keys do not appear in this column at all.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • ✘c. The 2 would be 0 if ITEM_ID were outside the key, and pk says nothing about indexing.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • ✔d. Correct: the numbers give each column's position within the single composite primary key.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Remember: In pragma_table_info, pk is a position inside the primary key, and any value above zero means the column is part of it.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Q4Cleaning up the KimTay archive table

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  A DBA created ITEM_ARCHIVE with a primary key and then added an index on its PRICE column, taking the catalog from 10 entries to 13. She now runs DROP TABLE ITEM_ARCHIVE. What does the catalog hold afterward?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • ✘a. An index cannot exist without its table; it is removed with the table, not left behind.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • ✔b. Correct: all three entries belonged to ITEM_ARCHIVE, so all three go when the table goes.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • ✘c. Nothing about an index is kept for reuse; the entry describes a structure that no longer exists.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • ✘d. DROP TABLE removes structure and rows together; DELETE is the statement that empties a table.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Remember: Dropping a table takes every catalog entry that belonged to it, indexes included.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Q5A late rule for KimTay's prices

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  KimTay wants PRICE > 0 enforced on the existing ITEM table, which already holds five rows. The database is SQLite. What has to happen?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • ✘a. SQLite has no ADD CONSTRAINT at any version; it expects a column definition after ADD and answers 'near "CONSTRAINT": syntax error'.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • ✘b. SQLite supports CHECK fully; what it lacks is a way to attach one after the table exists.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • ✘c. Only the one table has to be rebuilt, and the copy pattern from 6-8a does it inside a transaction.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • ✔d. Correct: create, copy, drop, rename, all in one transaction, is the portable way to add a constraint.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Remember: On SQLite a constraint has to be present at creation, so adding one means rebuilding that one table.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Q6A refused supplier at KimTay

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Inside an open transaction, a clerk inserts two valid suppliers and then a third whose LEAD_DAYS is 0, which a named CHECK refuses. What is the state of things immediately after the error?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • ✘a. A rejected statement undoes itself, not the whole transaction; the earlier work is still yours to commit.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • ✘b. Refusing a row means storing nothing; the engine never substitutes a value to make a row fit.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • ✔c. Correct: the failed INSERT changed nothing at all, and you may still COMMIT or ROLLBACK the rest.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • ✘d. There is no constraint log and no lock; the error is returned to you and the database moves on.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Remember: A constraint violation cancels one statement completely and leaves the surrounding transaction in your hands.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Q7The rep nobody can find

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  A practice table is created in the sandbox with REP_NUM CHAR(2) PRIMARY KEY, and an insert supplying NULL for REP_NUM is accepted. COUNT(*) returns 1 and COUNT(REP_NUM) returns 0. What is going on, and what is the fix?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • ✔a. Correct: SQLite allows this for backward compatibility, and NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY closes the hole.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • ✘b. COUNT(column) skipping nulls is exactly right; it is what proves no key value was stored.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • ✘c. The key is declared and working; it is only the null that SQLite failed to refuse.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • ✘d. The row is perfectly visible and permanent; nothing removes it on its own.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Remember: MySQL and Oracle make a primary key NOT NULL for you; on SQLite you write the two words yourself.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Q8An email column for KimTay suppliers

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  KimTay wants no two suppliers to share an email address, but a supplier that has not given one yet must still be storable. Which constraint fits?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • ✘a. A primary key identifies the row and would refuse the missing addresses you have to allow.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • ✔b. Correct: UNIQUE is the rule for no duplicates, and unlike a primary key it tolerates nulls.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • ✘c. NOT NULL requires a value to be present and says nothing whatever about duplicates.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • ✘d. A CHECK sees one row at a time and can never compare a value against other rows in the table.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Remember: UNIQUE is the constraint for no duplicates when the value may legitimately be missing.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Q9A view that updates itself at Downtown Aquarium and Pets

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  A view over CUSTOMER selects the customers with a balance above 1000 and returns three rows. A new customer is then inserted with a balance of 5000. Without anyone touching the view, it now returns four rows. Why?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • ✘a. A view holds no rows of its own, so there is no stored copy for anything to be appended to.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • ✘b. A view is not an index and creating one builds no structure over the base table at all.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • ✔c. Correct: the query runs at use time against current data, which is why a view is never stale.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • ✘d. Returning the fourth row is the view being right, not the view drifting out of date.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Remember: A view is a stored query, not stored data, so it always reflects the table as it is right now.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Q10Retiring an aviary cage at KimTay

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  With foreign keys enforced, KimTay wants item AV07 gone. AV07 appears on one line of invoice 50712. Which sequence completes without violating a constraint?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • ✔a. Correct: remove the child rows first and the parent then has nothing pointing at it.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • ✘b. This is refused: while the line exists, deleting the item would leave it pointing at nothing.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • ✘c. Cascading happens only when the foreign key was declared ON DELETE CASCADE, which this one was not.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • ✘d. It can be removed; the rule is about order, and clearing the children first is what makes it legal.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Remember: Referential integrity does not forbid deletions, it dictates their order: children first, then the parent.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Six exercises. The first four are on StayWell Student Accommodation, the last two return to KimTay Pet Supplies. Work each one in the sandbox before you open the solution. A sandbox keeps whatever you did to it until you press Reset, which reloads the sample data from scratch, so a mistake costs you nothing but one click. Every script below also carries the DROP ... IF EXISTS guards it needs to survive a second Run.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Read the data first

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  StayWell has two properties, Millbrook Commons (P100) managed by Diane Ortiz and Sycamore Court (P200) managed by Bruce Feldman, five rooms between them, four students, four leases, and four payments. Check the column names before you type: rooms carry ROOM_TYPE, MONTHLY_RENT, and MAX_OCCUPANTS, and ROOM has a two-column primary key of PROPERTY_ID and ROOM_NUM. Every column in every row is filled in.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Exercise 1: take inventory with the catalog

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  You have been handed the StayWell database with no documentation. List every table in it, then list the columns of LEASE with each column's type, whether it accepts nulls, and its position in the primary key. Run the starter before the solution and count how many entries are not tables.

PAYMENT has no index entry, and that is not a mistake: its key is PAYMENT_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, which SQLite stores as the row's own identifier, so no separate index is needed. LEASE comes back with seven columns and pk of 1 on LEASE_ID alone.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Exercise 2: create a view and an index, then find them in the catalog

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  StayWell wants a saved list of its double rooms, and searching by rent has become common enough to deserve an index. Create a view named DOUBLE_ROOMS over ROOM showing PROPERTY_ID, ROOM_NUM, and MONTHLY_RENT for rooms whose ROOM_TYPE is Double, create an index named ROOM_RENT_IDX on ROOM (MONTHLY_RENT), prove both exist by reading the catalog, then list the view. Use IF EXISTS on the drops so the script survives a second run.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  In this databaseclick a table to see its rows

Notice the tbl_name column: the index belongs to ROOM, while the view belongs to itself, because a view is not attached to any one table. The view lists the double at Millbrook Commons and the double at Sycamore Court, at 450 and 465.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Exercise 3: declare every constraint on a new table

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  StayWell is starting a room inspection programme, and the property managers do the inspecting. Build an INSPECTION table with INSPECTION_ID as the primary key, PROPERTY_ID, ROOM_NUM, INSPECTOR, and SCORE all required, a named CHECK keeping SCORE between 0 and 100, a named UNIQUE constraint allowing only one inspection per room, and a foreign key from the property and room pair to ROOM. Record P100 room 101 inspected by Ortiz scoring 92 and P200 room 202 inspected by Feldman scoring 88, list the table, then count what it added to the catalog.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  In this databaseclick a table to see its rows
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  A constraint that covers two columns cannot live on a column line. Give it its own line after the last column, and a name.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Three catalog entries this time: the table, the index enforcing the primary key, and a second index enforcing ONE_PER_ROOM. The starter version has only two, because it declared no uniqueness beyond the key. That difference is the clearest evidence you will see that a UNIQUE constraint is a working structure and not a comment.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Exercise 4: prove referential integrity, twice

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  A lease is entered for student S099, who has never existed. Run the first sandbox with enforcement off, watch the orphan lease go in, then remove it. Then run the second, which turns enforcement on and attempts the identical insert. The second one is meant to fail, and the error is the answer.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  SQL Sandbox · SQLite engine
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  In this databaseclick a table to see its rows
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Ask for the setting first. A 0 tells you what to expect from the insert that follows. The DELETE at the end tidies up, which is also what lets you press Run twice.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  SQL Sandbox · SQLite engine
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  In this databaseclick a table to see its rows
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  The starter proves the switch flipped. The solution is the same insert as the sandbox above, and it should now be refused.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  With enforcement off the lease is accepted, five leases appear, and the join from LEASE to STUDENT silently returns four of them. With enforcement on the answer is FOREIGN KEY constraint failed and nothing is written. The room part of the key was valid in both cases; P100 room 101 exists. It was the missing student that stopped it.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Exercise 5: add a constraint to a table that already has rows

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Back to KimTay. Nobody may be paid a commission rate above 0.25, and no commission total may be negative, but REP was created without either rule and SQLite has no ALTER TABLE ... ADD CONSTRAINT. Rebuild REP with the pattern from 6-8a: create REP_NEW carrying the same nine columns plus a NOT NULL primary key, two named CHECK constraints, and a default of 0 for COMMISSION; copy the three reps across; drop the original; rename the replacement. Wrap it in a transaction, then confirm from the catalog that the rules are now part of the table.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  SQL Sandbox · SQLite engine
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  In this databaseclick a table to see its rows
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  The starter shows the definition you are replacing. Copy it, add the rules, and remember that the INSERT will fail if any existing rep breaks one of them.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Kaiser, Hull, and Perez come through with rates of 0.05, 0.07, and 0.05, all inside the new range, which is why the copy succeeded. Read the final result carefully: the catalog now stores the rebuilt definition, with both named CHECK constraints in it, under the name REP, and the DBMS wrote that entry without being asked. Had one rep been on a rate of 0.30, the INSERT would have failed, the COMMIT would never have run, and the original table would still be there. That is why the transaction is not optional.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Exercise 6: audit the whole database from the catalog

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  A KimTay developer is planning to rename ITEM_ID and needs two facts before writing anything: how many columns each table has, and exactly which tables store a column called ITEM_ID. Produce both, with one query each, and do it without naming any table by hand except in the search itself.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  SQL Sandbox · SQLite engine
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  In this databaseclick a table to see its rows
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  The starter counts one table's columns. Put that count in the select list of a query over sqlite_master and it runs once per table.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Nine columns in CUSTOMER and REP, six in ITEM, four in INVOICE_LINE, three in INVOICE. The second query names INVOICE_LINE and ITEM, so the rename is two statements and a check of every view and report that spelled the old name. Neither query mentions a table list you typed, which means both stay correct the day somebody adds a sixth table.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  8-1 Using SQL in a Programming Environment

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Every statement you have written so far, you typed yourself. You opened a window, entered a SELECT, and read the rows that came back. That is a fine way to learn SQL and a fine way to answer a one-time question, but it is not how KimTay's business actually runs. Nobody at a pet supply distributor types a SELECT to look up a customer. A clerk clicks a name on a screen.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  The screen is a program. Behind that program is the same database and the same SQL. This lesson is about the seam between the two: what changes when SQL stops being typed and starts being sent.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Start with the data: the first program sends a query to CUSTOMER. Read the complete table first, including the two rows assigned to rep 20.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Source table: CUSTOMER — the data behind the first program query
