                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Tables you create by typing CREATE TABLE in the SQL Editor do not have PostgreSQL's Row Level Security turned on, and the Table Editor will show them with a red Unrestricted label. For this course that label is expected and is not an error -- it simply means the database is not filtering rows per end user, which is exactly what you want while doing KimTay exercises. Supabase also stopped exposing new public tables to a project's auto-generated Data API by default for projects created after 30 May 2026, so a project you create today is not publishing your coursework to the internet. Two rules anyway: do not put real personal data in a course project, and if you ever reuse this project for a public application, read Supabase's Row Level Security guide first.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Two different passwords -- do not mix them up

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              The sign-up in S-2 involves two separate passwords, and confusing them is the most common way students get stuck. Your account password is what you type at the Supabase sign-in page to reach the dashboard; if you sign up with GitHub instead, your GitHub login plays this role and there is no Supabase account password. Your database password is a different string, created when you create the project, and the SQL Editor never asks for it -- you only need it for a desktop client such as pgAdmin or psql (section S-5, optional) and for connection strings.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Supabase does not display the database password again after the project is created, so write it down when you create it. If you do lose it, you are not locked out of anything: you can set a new database password from the project's Database settings page in the dashboard, and your account login is unaffected either way.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              What you need before the next section

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Sign-up is mostly filling in a short form; Supabase then takes a few minutes to build your database before the SQL Editor will run anything. Budget about fifteen minutes and have these ready.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • An email address you can open right now -- Supabase sends a confirmation link you must click before you can sign in. (Signing up with a GitHub account also works and skips the password step; there is no Google option.)
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • A web browser: Chrome, Edge, Safari, or Firefox, all fine
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • A name for your project (kimtay is a good choice) and a region -- you will be asked for both, and picking the region geographically closest to you keeps queries fast
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • Somewhere to write down the database password the project-creation form asks you to set -- a password manager, a notes app, or paper. Supabase will not show it to you again, though you can reset it later if you lose it.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • About 15 minutes, including a few minutes of waiting while the project is created
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • No credit card. The Free plan does not ask for payment details.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • Nothing installed. If you want a desktop tool such as pgAdmin or psql later, section S-5 covers it, and it is optional.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              How you will know it worked

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              You are done with setup when you can do this, at the end of section S-2: open your project, click SQL Editor in the left-hand sidebar, type select version();, and click Run. Within a second or two a results panel appears below the editor showing one row in one column, and the text in it begins with the word PostgreSQL followed by a version number. That single line proves three things at once -- your account works, the project finished building, and you are talking to a real PostgreSQL database. If instead you see a spinner that never resolves, or a message that the project is still being set up, wait a minute and click Run again; the database is usually still provisioning.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              When you have those, continue to section S-2 and create your account.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              🔍 Check yourself: what Supabase is and what the Free plan gives you

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Pick an answer — the explanation opens right away.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Q1The laptop that died on Tuesday

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              A student has been building the KimTay tables in the sandbox on this page, on whichever lab computer is free that day. Twice now the tables have disappeared after the page was reloaded, and next week they will be working from home instead. They want one place to put the tables that survives both the reload and the change of computer.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • ✘a. The sandbox is deliberately throwaway -- the page says your tables are gone the moment you reload, and a shared lab machine gets reloaded by the next student.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • ✘b. A local install is permanent but lives on exactly one machine, so tables written on a lab computer are simply not there when you get home.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • ✔c. Correct -- the page puts Supabase in between the other two: a real database that keeps your data and that you reach from any computer with a web browser.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • ✘d. Keeping your own copy of the SQL is good advice because the Free plan has no backups, but a local install and a Supabase project both do keep data on their own.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Remember: Sandbox for throwaway experiments, local install for one machine, Supabase when the data has to outlive the tab and the computer.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Q2The second project that would not start

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              A student already has one active Free-plan project holding KimTay and now wants a second project for a personal experiment. A classmate says to just create another organization to get more projects, and adds that the storage cap is shared between them anyway.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • ✔a. Correct -- the page states the 2-active-project limit is a total across every organization where you are an Owner or Administrator, and that paused projects do not count against it.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • ✘b. This is exactly the misconception the page calls out: the limit is not two per organization, so extra organizations do not raise your total.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • ✘c. The 500 MB is per project, not shared, and the whole KimTay database is only a few kilobytes, so storage is never the pinch point here.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • ✘d. Backwards -- the Free plan is the one carrying the limits (2 active projects, 500 MB each, pausing after a week idle), and it never asks for a credit card.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Remember: Free plan: 2 active projects account-wide, 500 MB per project, no credit card -- plan on one project for KimTay and keep the other slot free.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Q3The project that went quiet over the break

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              A student returns from a two-week break, opens the Supabase dashboard, and finds the KimTay project marked as paused. Convinced a semester of work has been thrown away, they start hunting for the CREATE TABLE script to build everything again.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • ✘a. Pausing is not deletion -- the page is explicit that tables, rows, and settings are all preserved on disk while the project is asleep.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • ✘b. Seven days is the inactivity window that triggers a pause, not a deadline for restoring; the page gives you a one-year window to resume from the dashboard.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • ✘c. Resuming has nothing to do with backups -- it is a dashboard button, and the Free plan's missing backups only matter if you damage or delete the data yourself.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • ✔d. Correct -- open the dashboard, click your organization, click the paused project, then Resume project and confirm; restoring takes a few minutes.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Remember: A pause is reversible for one year. Regular database use is the dependable way to avoid it, and visiting the project after a warning can prevent the pending pause.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              🧩 Sort the need into the right place to run SQL

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Click a card, then click where it belongs.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Each card describes something a student in this course actually needs. Drop it on the one place from the S-1 table that fits it best -- the throwaway sandbox on this page, a database installed on one computer, or a Supabase project.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    0 / 6 placed

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    S-2 Create your Supabase project

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    By the end of this section you will have a real PostgreSQL database running on the internet, owned by you, that you can reach from a browser in about ten minutes and without installing anything. Nothing here costs money -- Supabase's Free plan does not ask for a credit card. You will not create any tables yet; the goal is an empty, healthy database and a saved password. Read step 6 carefully, because it is the one step students skip and the only one that is genuinely painful to undo.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    📝
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Before you start

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    You need three things: a web browser, an email address you can check right now, and about ten minutes. You do not need to install anything, you do not need to open a terminal, and you do not need a credit card. If you already have a GitHub account, signing in with it saves a step. Before you begin, open a second window with your password manager (1Password, Bitwarden, Apple Passwords, your browser's built-in one) or, if you have none, your computer's notes app -- step 6 asks you to save something the instant it appears, and you do not want to be hunting for a place to put it.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    1

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Create your Supabase account

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Go to https://supabase.com/dashboard/sign-up. You have two options. Click Continue with GitHub and authorize Supabase -- fastest if you already have a GitHub account. Or type an email address and a password into the form and submit it; Supabase then emails you a confirmation link, and the account is not active until you click it. Use an email you actually check, and if the message has not arrived in a couple of minutes look in your spam or junk folder. The account password must be at least 8 characters with an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter, a number, and a special character. Important: this password logs you in to the Supabase website. It is not the database password you create in step 6. They are two different secrets and you will end up needing both.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    2

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Land in an organization

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    An organization is the container that holds your projects, and later your billing and any teammates. New accounts normally get one created automatically with you as the Owner, so there is usually nothing to do here. If instead Supabase shows you a form asking you to create one, fill it in: any name works (keiser-db or your own name is fine) and choose the Free plan when asked. One organization is all this course needs.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    3

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Start a new project

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    From your organization's Projects page, click the New project button. If your dashboard is empty and you cannot find the button, go straight to https://supabase.com/dashboard/new/_ -- the _ on the end tells Supabase to use whichever organization you were last in. Either way you land on a page headed Create a new project.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    4

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Check the Organization field

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    The first field on the form is Organization. If you only have one, it is already filled in and you can move on. If you somehow have more than one, pick the free organization from step 2 -- creating the project under the wrong organization is the kind of mistake that turns into a surprise bill later.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    5

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Name the project

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    In the Project name field, type something you will still recognize in three weeks. kimtay is a good choice, since KimTay Pet Supplies is the database you are about to build. This name is only a label in the dashboard -- it does not become the name of the database (that is always postgres), and you can rename it later under Project Settings then General.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    6

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Generate the database password, then save it before you touch anything else

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Find the field labelled Database password. Directly beneath it is a password-strength meter with a small Generate a password link -- click that link. Supabase fills the field with a long random password, shown as dots because it is a password field, and a copy icon appears at the right-hand edge of the field. Click the copy icon, then immediately paste the password into your password manager or notes app. Give the entry a name like "Supabase kimtay DATABASE password" so you can tell it apart from your supabase.com login. Do not paste it into a file inside a project folder you will push to GitHub, and do not plan to retype it from memory. Do not click away from this form until it is saved somewhere -- the moment you create the project, the dashboard's own Database settings page will tell you that "the database password isn't viewable after creation."

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    7

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Choose the region closest to you

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Open the Region dropdown. The top group is labelled General regions and holds a few broad choices; below it is a longer list of specific AWS data centers, city by city. Students in Florida should pick East US (North Virginia), which appears in both groups -- either entry is fine. The rest of the list is for people in other parts of the world. Pick the location physically nearest to where you sit.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    8

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Leave the Security options at their defaults

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Below the region is a Security block with checkboxes such as Enable Data API, Automatically expose new tables, and Enable automatic RLS. Accept whatever Supabase has pre-selected. This course drives the database from the SQL Editor and from desktop tools that connect as the postgres user, and none of these settings affect either path, so there is nothing to change and nothing you can break here. If you also see options named High availability or Compute size, leave them off or at the smallest default -- those are paid add-ons.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    9

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Click Create new project and wait

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Press the Create new project button at the bottom of the form. The dashboard opens immediately and shows the project in a setting-up state. Leave the tab open and give it a minute or two -- see "What the wait is" below.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    What each field on the New project form actually decides
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    FieldWhat it setsChangeable later?
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    OrganizationWhich container -- and therefore which plan and billing account -- owns the projectYes -- a project can be transferred to another organization
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Project nameA label in your dashboard onlyYes, any time, under Project Settings then General
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Database passwordThe password for the Postgres user named postgres, which outside tools connect withOnly by resetting it at Database then Settings, which breaks every saved connection string
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    RegionThe physical AWS data center your database runs inNo -- you would create a new project in the new region and migrate the data across
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Security checkboxesWhether the auto-generated REST API can see new tables, and whether Row Level Security is switched on automaticallyYes -- adjustable later per project and per table

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Why the password step is the one that bites people

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    That generated password is the credential every outside tool uses to connect directly to your database -- psql, pgAdmin, TablePlus, or an application you write later. Specifically, it is the password for the Postgres user named postgres. Supabase does not keep a readable copy of it: Postgres stores only a hash, so there is nothing for the dashboard to show you. The dashboard says so itself, in plain words, on the page where you would go looking: "The database password isn't viewable after creation." There is no reveal button anywhere.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    ⚠️
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Shown once, never shown again

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    If you lose the database password you cannot recover it -- you can only reset it. The reset lives in the left sidebar under Database, then Settings, in the Database password section (Reset database password). A reset is not the end of the world, but the new password invalidates every connection string you have already saved in a tool or a script, so you will be re-pasting it in several places. Save it the first time. And keep it clearly labelled: this is a different password from the one you use to sign in to supabase.com, and resetting the wrong one does not help.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    What the region choice actually affects

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    The region is the physical data center where your Postgres server lives. It affects one thing you will notice: round-trip time. Every query you run travels from your laptop to that data center and back, so a database in Virginia answers a student in Florida in a few dozen milliseconds, while one in Sydney adds a visible pause -- closer to a quarter of a second -- to every single statement. It does not change the SQL, the data types, the price, or the Free-plan limits.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    "Closest to you" is the right default for coursework because you are the only user. In a real product you would pick the region closest to your users instead, which is not always where you are. Pick carefully now: a project is bound to its region at the hardware level on every plan, not just the free one. Supabase's own guidance is that the only way to change region is to create a new project in the region you want and migrate the data across -- so for coursework, a wrong choice means building the schema again.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    What the wait is

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Supabase is provisioning a dedicated Postgres instance for you, creating the default database (it is called postgres), and starting the API, authentication, and storage services that sit in front of it. The dashboard's own wording is that your project will be ready in a few minutes; in practice it is usually one to three. You do not need to reload the page -- the status updates itself, moving from a setting-up state through Starting to an active project. If you open the SQL Editor too early and a query fails with a connection error, wait thirty seconds and run it again rather than assuming something is broken.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Confirm it worked

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Once the setup banner clears, click SQL Editor in the left sidebar. A blank query tab normally opens by itself. If the editor is showing something else instead, click the small + button at the top of the SQL Editor's snippet list -- hovering it shows the tooltip Create a new query -- and choose Create a new snippet. Type or paste the statement below into the editor, then press the Run button, or use Cmd+Enter on a Mac and Ctrl+Enter on Windows.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    -- SELECT version(): a query with no FROM clause and no table involved. It asks
--   the server to describe itself, and the row that comes back proves three
--   things at once - you are connected, the connection works both ways, and the
--   engine underneath is PostgreSQL rather than SQLite or MySQL.
SELECT version();

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    version() is a built-in PostgreSQL function that reports the server's version string, and this is about the smallest valid statement that proves a database is answering you. You should get a results grid with exactly one row and one column named version, whose value begins with the word PostgreSQL followed by a version number and some build details. The details do not matter; any output at all means your database is alive and you are talking to it. If you instead get a red error about the connection or about the project not being ready, the project is still starting -- wait half a minute and press Run again.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • The project appears in your dashboard in an active state -- not Paused, not Starting, not still setting up.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • The left sidebar shows Table Editor, SQL Editor, Database, Authentication, and Storage (there are more items below those, which is normal).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • SELECT version(); in the SQL Editor returns one row, in a column named version, whose value starts with PostgreSQL.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • Table Editor opens on the public schema and offers to create your first table. An empty table list is the correct result here -- you have not created any yet.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • Your database password is saved outside any folder you push to GitHub, somewhere you can find it in a week, and labelled clearly enough that you will know it is the *database* password and not your supabase.com login.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • You can get back to everything above by visiting https://supabase.com/dashboard and signing in. Nothing you just built lives only on this computer.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    ⚠️
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Never commit the database password or a secret API key

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Two kinds of secret belong to this project. The first is the database password you just saved. The second is your project's secret API key, a string beginning sb_secret_, which you will meet later under Project Settings then API Keys (it is also surfaced in the project's Connect dialog). Older tutorials call this the service_role key; Supabase stopped issuing service_role and anon keys to newly created projects in November 2025, so on a project you create today the sb_secret_ key is the equivalent, and the safe-to-share public one is sb_publishable_. Both the database password and the secret key grant full control of the database and both bypass every Row Level Security rule. Do not paste either into a file you commit to GitHub, a shared Google Doc, a Discord or group chat, a screenshot, or a homework submission. Bots scan public repositories for exactly these strings within minutes of a push. If you ever suspect one leaked: reset the database password at Database then Settings, and delete and recreate the secret key at Project Settings then API Keys.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    📝
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Free-plan facts worth knowing now

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    The Free plan gives you up to 2 free projects across all of your organizations, with 500 MB of database storage each -- far more than the KimTay data will ever need -- and it does not require a credit card. Supabase pauses Free-plan projects with too little user database activity over a 7-day window; its guidance says a few requests to the database each day are typically enough to keep a project active. Supabase emails the owner roughly a week before a pause and says visiting the project in the dashboard after that warning can prevent it. A paused project keeps its data and configuration: select it, click Resume project, and wait for it to return. You have up to one year to resume it.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    🔍 Check yourself: creating the project without creating a problem

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Pick an answer — the explanation opens right away.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Q1The password nobody wrote down

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    On the New project form a student clicked Generate a password, saw a field full of dots, and moved straight on to the region dropdown without copying anything. Two weeks later they want to connect pgAdmin and are clicking through the dashboard looking for somewhere to read the password back.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • ✘a. There is no reveal button anywhere -- Postgres stores only a hash, and the dashboard itself says the database password is not viewable after creation.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • ✔b. Correct -- reset it in the Database password section under Database then Settings, then expect to re-paste the new one into every tool that had the old one.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • ✘c. These are two different secrets: the account password signs you in to supabase.com, while the database password belongs to the Postgres user named postgres.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • ✘d. Losing the database password locks you out of nothing -- your account login is unaffected, and the cost of a reset is re-pasting the new password into your saved connection strings, not any of your data.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Remember: Copy the generated database password into a password manager before you leave the form, and label it so you never confuse it with your supabase.com login.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Q2The quarter-second pause

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Sitting in Florida, a student scrolled the Region dropdown and picked a Sydney data center because the name looked interesting. Every statement in the SQL Editor now hesitates noticeably before answering, and they want to move the project to East US (North Virginia).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • ✘a. The project name really is renameable there, but the field table on the page marks Region as the one choice you cannot change later.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • ✘b. The region is the physical AWS data center your Postgres server lives in, and that distance is exactly what adds the visible round-trip delay to every statement.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • ✘c. A project is bound to its region at the hardware level on every plan, not just the Free one, so paying more does not move it.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • ✔d. Correct -- Supabase's own guidance is to create a new project in the region you want and migrate the data across, which for coursework means building the schema again.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Remember: Region affects round-trip time only, but it is permanent -- pick the data center nearest you before you click Create new project.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Q3The repo that was scanned in minutes

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    A student is about to push their whole course folder to a public GitHub repository. Inside it are a notes file containing the project's database password and a config file holding a key that begins sb_secret_. A classmate tells them only one of the two is really sensitive.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • ✔a. Correct -- the page says both the database password and the sb_secret_ key grant full control and bypass RLS, and that bots scan public repositories for these strings within minutes of a push.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • ✘b. The safe-to-share key is the sb_publishable_ one; sb_secret_ (called service_role in older tutorials) is a full-control secret and must stay out of the repository.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • ✘c. A filename hides nothing in a public repository -- every file in it is readable by anyone, and automated scanners read them fast.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • ✘d. Unrestricted only means Row Level Security is off, and on projects created on or after 30 May 2026 a new public table is invisible to the Data API until you write an explicit GRANT.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Remember: The database password and the sb_secret_ key are equally dangerous -- keep both out of repositories, chats, screenshots, and homework submissions.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    S-3 Run your first SQL in the Supabase SQL Editor

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    This is the section where the account you made starts paying off. In the next ten minutes you will open Supabase's SQL Editor, prove your connection works with a one-line query, then build the KimTay REP table and load the three reps -- the same table you built in Module 3, except this time the rows live on a real Postgres server and are still there tomorrow. Everything happens in your browser. You will not open a terminal, install anything, or type a password at a command prompt.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    📝
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Before you start

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    You need the free Supabase account and the project you created in the previous section, and you need to be signed in. If you just created the project, look at its status on the dashboard first -- a brand-new project spends a minute or two setting up, and SQL run against it before it is ready will fail with a connection error rather than a SQL error. Wait until the project opens normally and stops saying it is being set up.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Open the SQL Editor and prove the connection works

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    1

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Open your project

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Go to supabase.com/dashboard and click the project you created. If you belong to more than one organization, pick the organization first, then the project. You land on the project dashboard, with a narrow icon sidebar down the left edge. How you know it worked: the project name appears at the top of the page and the sidebar is visible.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    2

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Click SQL Editor

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    In the left sidebar, click SQL Editor. On a narrow window the sidebar collapses to icons only -- hover over each icon and the name appears in a tooltip; SQL Editor is the one shaped like a small terminal window. If you are already signed in, the address supabase.com/dashboard/project/_/sql/new also works: the _ is a placeholder that Supabase swaps for whichever project you used last, so check the project name at the top before you run anything.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    3

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Start a new query

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Click New query. You get an empty text area on top and an empty results panel underneath. This is where every statement in this section goes. How you know it worked: there is a tab or entry named Untitled query, and the text area is empty and accepts typing.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    4

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Run one line

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Click inside the text area, type the statement below, then click the green Run button (or press Cmd+Enter on a Mac, Ctrl+Enter on Windows or Linux). The results panel replaces its empty state with a small table.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    -- SELECT version(): a query with no FROM clause and no table involved. It asks
--   the server to describe itself, and the row that comes back proves three
--   things at once - you are connected, the connection works both ways, and the
--   engine underneath is PostgreSQL rather than SQLite or MySQL.
SELECT version();

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    The results panel shows one row with one column, headed version, holding a long line of text that begins with the word PostgreSQL followed by a version number. The line is wider than the panel, so you may have to scroll the results sideways to read all of it -- you do not need to. Seeing PostgreSQL at the front is your proof: your browser reached a real Postgres server, the server ran your SQL, and it sent an answer back. Nothing was installed on your computer to make that happen.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    📝
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    If you see a red error instead

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    An error that mentions the project being paused means Supabase put a Free plan project to sleep, which it does after roughly a week of very little activity. Go back to supabase.com/dashboard, click the project, click Resume project, and confirm. Give it a minute or two, then run SELECT version(); again. If instead you get a network or connection error on a brand-new project, it is still finishing setup -- wait a minute and retry. A red error that quotes your own SQL back at you is a different thing entirely: that is a typo, and the message names the line and position to look at.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Build the REP table

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Clear the editor first: click anywhere inside the text area, press Cmd+A on a Mac or Ctrl+A on Windows or Linux to select everything, then press Delete. Now paste the CREATE TABLE below. This is the exact KimTay REP definition from Module 3. Postgres accepts CHAR, VARCHAR, and DECIMAL with the same meanings you learned there, so nothing has to change -- with one difference worth knowing: Postgres actually enforces the sizes. The browser sandbox lets a 40-character name sit happily in a VARCHAR(15); Postgres rejects it with a value too long error. That is the stricter, more realistic behavior, and it is one of the reasons to move here.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    -- CREATE TABLE: the same statement you wrote in Module 3, run against a real
--   PostgreSQL server this time instead of the in-browser sandbox.
CREATE TABLE REP (

    -- CHAR(2) and PRIMARY KEY behave identically in PostgreSQL.
    REP_NUM      CHAR(2)      PRIMARY KEY,

    -- VARCHAR(15) NOT NULL - portable across all three engines in this course.
