    LAST_NAME    VARCHAR(15)  NOT NULL,
    FIRST_NAME   VARCHAR(15)  NOT NULL,

    -- Nullable columns: no rule attached, so these may be left empty.
    STREET       VARCHAR(20),
    CITY         VARCHAR(15),
    STATE        CHAR(2),

    -- CHAR(5), not a number, so a leading zero in a ZIP survives.
    ZIP          CHAR(5),

    -- DECIMAL is exact money in PostgreSQL too (it is a synonym for NUMERIC).
    COMMISSION   DECIMAL(8,2),
    RATE         DECIMAL(4,2)
);

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Click Run. A successful CREATE TABLE returns no rows, so the results panel says Success. No rows returned. That is what you want -- it is not an empty result that failed quietly, it is the normal response to a statement that changes the database rather than asking it a question. The table now exists on the server, and it will still exist after you close the browser.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    📝
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Why the table shows up as lowercase rep

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Postgres folds unquoted names to lower case, so REP is stored as rep and REP_NUM as rep_num. You can keep writing your SQL in upper case exactly as the course does -- Postgres folds your query the same way, so it still matches. The only rule to remember is not to wrap a name in double quotes unless you are willing to type those quotes every time afterwards: CREATE TABLE "REP" really does create a table whose name is upper case, and from then on SELECT * FROM REP; will fail with relation "rep" does not exist.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    💡
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    How to start over if you run something twice

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Unlike the sandbox on this page, this database remembers. Running the CREATE TABLE a second time fails with relation "rep" already exists, and running the inserts twice fails with duplicate key value violates unique constraint "rep_pkey" -- both are the server correctly refusing to duplicate work, not a broken setup. To wipe the slate and rebuild, run DROP TABLE IF EXISTS REP; and then run the CREATE TABLE and the inserts again. Supabase shows a confirmation dialog before it runs a destructive statement such as DROP or DELETE; read it, then confirm.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Insert the three reps

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Clear the editor again (Cmd+A or Ctrl+A, then Delete) and paste all three INSERT statements. Notice each one ends with a semicolon -- that is how the editor knows where one statement stops and the next begins. All three go in one run.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    -- INSERT INTO ... VALUES: three separate statements, one per row. Naming the
--   columns each time is longer to type and much easier to check.
INSERT INTO REP (REP_NUM, LAST_NAME, FIRST_NAME, STREET, CITY, STATE, ZIP, COMMISSION, RATE)

-- The values, in the same order as the column list. Text in SINGLE quotes -
--   PostgreSQL reads double quotes as an identifier, not as text.
VALUES ('20', 'Kaiser', 'Valerie', '624 Randall Dr.', 'Maple Grove', 'OH', '44601', 21560.00, 0.05);

-- The second rep. Each statement is independent: if one fails the others still run.
INSERT INTO REP (REP_NUM, LAST_NAME, FIRST_NAME, STREET, CITY, STATE, ZIP, COMMISSION, RATE)
VALUES ('35', 'Hull', 'Richard', '313 Palma Dr.', 'Maple Grove', 'OH', '44601', 39355.00, 0.07);

-- The third. Notice REP_NUM is quoted every time, because the column is CHAR(2).
INSERT INTO REP (REP_NUM, LAST_NAME, FIRST_NAME, STREET, CITY, STATE, ZIP, COMMISSION, RATE)
VALUES ('65', 'Perez', 'Juan', '2632 Marshall Ave.', 'Brookville', 'OH', '44403', 23764.00, 0.05);

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Run it. You get Success. No rows returned again -- inserts change the database, they do not answer a question, so there is nothing to show. Now ask for the data back:

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    -- SELECT *: read everything back. Three rows means all three INSERTs committed
--   to a real server - the data is now on Supabase, not in your browser.
SELECT * FROM REP ORDER BY REP_NUM;

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Three rows: Kaiser, Hull, Perez. The ORDER BY is there on purpose -- a plain SELECT * FROM REP; also returns all three, but no database promises you a particular order unless you ask for one, so do not read anything into the order you happen to get. Same result as the sandbox on this page, with one difference that matters: close this tab, come back next week, run it again, and the three rows are still there.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    💡
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Run only part of your script

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    If you highlight some text before clicking Run (or pressing Cmd+Enter / Ctrl+Enter), the editor runs only the highlighted statements and ignores the rest. That is the fastest way to work through a long script: keep every statement in one query and highlight just the line you want to test. If nothing is highlighted, everything in the editor runs, top to bottom -- which is also the usual reason a DROP you thought was safely parked at the bottom of the file suddenly runs.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    The sandbox on this page vs. the Supabase SQL Editor
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    WhatSandbox on this pageSupabase SQL Editor
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    EngineSQLite, running inside your browserPostgreSQL, running on a server
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Your dataGone when you reload the pageKept until you delete it
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Column sizesVARCHAR(15) is not enforcedVARCHAR(15) is enforced; oversized values are rejected
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Saving workCopy the text out yourselfSaved automatically as a snippet you can rename
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    What runsEverything in the boxYour selection, or everything if nothing is selected
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Who you areThe only user there isAn administrator, so row-security rules never hide anything from you here

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Name the query so you can find it again

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Supabase already saved this query for you -- every query you run in the SQL Editor is kept as a snippet in your project, which is why the left-hand list is filling up with entries called Untitled query. The part you have to do is give it a name. Click the query's name above the editor, or open the ... menu next to its entry in the left-hand list and choose the rename option, and call it KimTay - create REP. Clicking a snippet in that list loads it back into the editor. This is the Supabase version of the habit Module 3 taught you with saved .sql script files: write it once, keep it, run it again when you need to rebuild. Snippets live in your Supabase account, not in the database, so they are not part of your data and will not appear in a backup of your tables -- keep a copy of anything you cannot afford to lose.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    The point-and-click alternative: Table Editor

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    You do not have to use SQL to make a table here. Click Table Editor in the left sidebar, then New table, give it a name, click Save, and add columns one at a time with New column -- pick a name and a data type, then Save. Your rep table is already in that list; if you do not see it, reload the page, because the Table Editor caches the table list and does not always notice a table created in another tab. The Table Editor is a reasonable way to look at data you already have, and clicking through a table's rows is easier than typing a SELECT every time. It is a poor way to learn, though, because the design decisions you made in Module 2 get buried in a form instead of written down in a script you can save, read, and hand to someone else. Build with SQL, browse with the Table Editor.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    ⚠️
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Two separate switches control who can reach a table from outside the dashboard

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    The first is Row Level Security, or RLS, which decides which rows a request is allowed to see. The New table form in the Table Editor has an Enable Row Level Security (RLS) box that is ticked by default, and a table with RLS on and no policies returns zero rows to any app connecting with your project's publishable key (the anon key on older projects) -- while the Table Editor still shows every row, because the dashboard connects as an administrator. That mismatch is the single most common "my app is broken" moment in Supabase, and the app is behaving exactly as configured. A table you create with SQL, like the REP table you just built, starts with RLS off, and Supabase marks it in the dashboard with an Unrestricted badge and an RLS disabled in public warning. The second switch is Postgres grants, which decide whether a role may touch the table at all, and this default changed during 2026: projects created before May 30, 2026 automatically granted select, insert, update, and delete on every new table in the public schema to the anon, authenticated, and service_role roles, so an RLS-off table genuinely was readable by anything holding the publishable key. Projects created on or after May 30, 2026 do not do that -- a new table in public is invisible to the Data API until you write an explicit GRANT -- and Supabase applies the same setting to all remaining older projects on October 30, 2026. None of this changes anything you did in this section, because the SQL Editor talks to the database directly with administrator privileges. It matters the moment you point an application at the database. Before you put real data in any table in the public schema, run ALTER TABLE REP ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; and write at least one policy, then grant only the access each role actually needs.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • SELECT version(); returns one row in a column headed version, starting with the word PostgreSQL
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • CREATE TABLE REP (...) reports Success. No rows returned
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • The three INSERT statements run with no errors
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • SELECT * FROM REP ORDER BY REP_NUM; returns exactly three rows: Kaiser, Hull, Perez
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • You can recover from a mistake: DROP TABLE IF EXISTS REP; followed by the create and the inserts rebuilds the table from scratch
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • Your query is renamed from Untitled query and you can find it again in the SQL Editor's left-hand list
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • rep appears in the Table Editor's table list, and you can explain why it is lowercase
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • You can explain why the SQL Editor shows you rows that an app using the publishable key might not see

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    🔍 Check yourself: running SQL in the Supabase SQL Editor

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Pick an answer — the explanation opens right away.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Q1The first query of the semester

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    A brand-new project has finally stopped saying it is being set up. Before typing any CREATE TABLE, a student wants one quick check that the browser really is talking to a live Postgres server. The group chat offers several ways to test it.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • ✘a. SHOW DATABASES; is a MySQL habit that does not belong here -- your project already is the database, and it is always named postgres.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • ✘b. The blank query tab is just the dashboard's own interface loading; the page warns that a query run too early still fails with a connection error and should be retried in thirty seconds, so the tab proves nothing about the server.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • ✔c. Correct -- version() is a built-in PostgreSQL function, and one row in a column headed version starting with PostgreSQL proves your account, the project, and the database all work.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • ✘d. A red error that quotes your own SQL back at you is a typo, which is a completely different problem from a connection error or a project still provisioning.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Remember: SELECT version(); is the smallest statement that proves a database is answering you -- run it before you build anything.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Q2The DROP parked at the bottom

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    A student keeps their entire KimTay script in one query tab, with DROP TABLE IF EXISTS REP; sitting at the bottom for later. Wanting to re-run just the three INSERT statements, they click into the editor, highlight nothing, and press Run.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • ✘a. There is no cursor-line rule in this editor -- it runs your selection, and with nothing selected it runs the entire contents of the box.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • ✔b. Correct -- the page names this as the usual reason a DROP you thought was safely parked at the bottom suddenly runs, though Supabase does confirm before destructive statements.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • ✘c. Highlighting is optional, not required: selecting text is how you run only part of a long script, which is the fast way to test one line at a time.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • ✘d. Semicolons tell the editor where one statement stops and the next begins, and all of them run in order -- which is why all three INSERT statements can go in a single run.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Remember: Selection wins: highlight the statements you want, because an empty selection means the whole editor runs, DROP included.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Q3The table that is not in the list

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    A student builds REP with CREATE TABLE in the SQL Editor and gets Success. No rows returned. Switching to a tab that already had Table Editor open, they see no sign of the table, and a classmate tells them to just rebuild it with the New table form instead.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • ✘a. The page says the opposite -- the rep table you just built with SQL is already in that list, and the standing advice is build with SQL, browse with the Table Editor.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • ✘b. Success. No rows returned is the correct response to a statement that changes the database rather than asking it a question -- the table does exist.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • ✘c. Postgres folds unquoted names to lower case, so CREATE TABLE REP stores a table named rep; only a double-quoted name keeps its capitals.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • ✔d. Correct -- the page warns that the Table Editor caches the table list and does not always notice a table created in another tab, so reload the page.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Remember: Build with SQL and browse with the Table Editor -- and remember unquoted names arrive in the list folded to lower case.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    S-4 Connect from your own machine: Mac

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    So far you have run SQL inside a browser tab. This section gets your Mac talking to your Supabase database directly, using a real SQL client that you own. The payoff is that you can open a saved script, run it against your own KimTay tables, and see results without the Supabase dashboard in the way. You will do two things: copy one connection string, then hand that string to a client. Pick either the point-and-click route (a GUI app) or the terminal route. You do not need both.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    📝
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Before you start

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    You need three things: (1) the Supabase project you created earlier in this course, with your KimTay tables already loaded; (2) the database password you set when you created that project, or the willingness to reset it -- resetting is safe and takes about a minute; (3) about 15 minutes. Nothing here costs money. If you are on the terminal route, you also need macOS 14 (Sonoma) or newer, which is what Homebrew supports today.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Step 1: copy the connection string

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    A connection string is one line of text that tells a client where the database lives and who you are. Supabase generates it for you. You never type it from memory, and you never copy one out of a tutorial -- every project has its own.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    1

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Open your project

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Go to supabase.com/dashboard and click the project you created for this course.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    2

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Click Connect

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    The Connect button sits at the top of the project dashboard and opens a panel. This is where connection strings now live. Older tutorials send you to Project Settings then Database for the connection string -- that is out of date.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    3

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Choose the connection that reaches your network

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    The panel lists Direct connection, Transaction pooler, and Session pooler. For a desktop client or psql, use the direct connection when your network supports IPv6 or your project has the IPv4 add-on. On an IPv4-only network, copy the Session pooler instead.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    4

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Paste it somewhere safe

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Paste it into a plain text file for a moment. It looks like postgresql://postgres.abcdefghijklmnopqrst:[YOUR-PASSWORD]@aws-1-us-east-1.pooler.supabase.com:5432/postgres. Two parts of that are yours alone: abcdefghijklmnopqrst is your project reference, and the host name encodes your project's region. The [YOUR-PASSWORD] part is a placeholder -- replace it, square brackets and all, with the database password you set when you created the project.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    ⚠️
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Do not copy the example host

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    The host in the example above is an example. Yours will differ in both the region (us-east-1, eu-central-1, ap-southeast-2, ...) and the number after aws- -- Supabase issues aws-0-, aws-1-, and others, and there is no way to guess which one your project got. Always paste the host from your own Connect panel. Copying a host from a tutorial is the single most common reason a connection never resolves.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    📝
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Why you may need the session pooler

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    The direct endpoint uses IPv6 unless the project has the IPv4 add-on. If your home or campus network is IPv4-only, use the shared Session pooler: it is reachable over IPv4 and suits a persistent desktop-client session. The direct connection remains the preferred choice for native Postgres tools when your network can reach it.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Which connection to pick for this course
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    OptionHostPortUse it for
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Direct connectiondb.[PROJECT-REF].supabase.co5432Native Postgres tools and single sessions when IPv6 works, or when the project has the IPv4 add-on.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Session pooleraws-N-[REGION].pooler.supabase.com5432Persistent desktop clients on IPv4-only networks.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Transaction pooleraws-N-[REGION].pooler.supabase.com6543Serverless and edge functions. Does not support prepared statements. Not this course.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    ⚠️
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Forgot the password

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    The database password is shown only while you are creating the project, and Supabase cannot show it to you again. If you did not save it, do not guess -- reset it. In the dashboard's left sidebar click Database, then Settings (the page URL ends in /database/settings), and use the reset-password control there. Set the new password, then go back to Connect and copy the string again. Resetting does not touch your tables or data.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Step 2 (route A): connect with a GUI client

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    A GUI client gives you a window with your tables on the left and a query editor on the right. Two are worth your time on a Mac. Pick one -- installing both just doubles the setup.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    TablePlus

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Download from tableplus.com/download. It is fast, quiet, and the easiest of the two to learn. It is paid software, but the trial never expires; it limits you to 2 open tabs and 2 open windows at a time, which is plenty for this course. Requires macOS 10.13 or newer and runs on both Intel and Apple Silicon from a single download. Best pick if your Mac is older.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    pgAdmin 4

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Download from pgadmin.org/download/pgadmin-4-macos. It is free and open source, built by the PostgreSQL community, with no usage limits. The interface is busier and it runs inside a browser-like window, so expect more clicking. There are separate Intel and Apple Silicon downloads -- pick the one matching your Mac (Apple menu, About This Mac, look at Chip or Processor). Current releases require macOS 13 (Ventura) or newer.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Both apps ask for the same five pieces of information, and all five are sitting inside the connection string you copied. Read the string left to right: after postgresql:// (Supabase sometimes writes postgres:// -- same thing) comes the user, then the first : and the password, then @ and the host, then the last : and the port, then / and the database name.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Filling in a new connection from your string
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    FieldWhat to enterExample
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    HostEverything between @ and the last :aws-1-us-east-1.pooler.supabase.com
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    PortThe number after the last :5432
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    DatabaseThe word after the final /postgres
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    UserEverything between // and the first : after itpostgres.abcdefghijklmnopqrst
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    PasswordYour project database passwordthe value you set or reset -- no square brackets
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    ⚠️
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Keep the dot in the user name

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    On the session pooler the user name is postgres, then a dot, then your project reference -- for example postgres.abcdefghijklmnopqrst. Students often shorten it to plain postgres and get the error Tenant or user not found. Copy the whole thing, dot included.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    In TablePlus: click Create a new connection..., choose PostgreSQL, give it a name like KimTay, fill the five fields, click Test (the fields turn green when they are reachable), then Connect. If TablePlus offers an SSL mode option, PREFERRED works and REQUIRED is stricter; either connects.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    In pgAdmin 4: right-click Servers in the left tree, choose Register then Server.... On the General tab put any nickname you like in Name. On the Connection tab, note that pgAdmin uses slightly different labels -- Host name/address, Port, Maintenance database (this is the Database field: enter postgres), Username, and Password. Tick Save password? so you do not retype it. pgAdmin defaults to an SSL mode of prefer, which already encrypts the connection to Supabase; if you want to force it, go to the Parameters tab, click +, choose SSL mode, and set it to require.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    💡
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    How to know the GUI worked

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    You should see your KimTay tables, not just a connected server. In TablePlus the left sidebar lists them under the public schema. In pgAdmin, expand the server, then Databases, then postgres, then Schemas, then public, then Tables -- your course tables are there. If you connect but see no tables, you are connected to the right server but looking at the wrong schema; make sure you are under public, not auth or storage. Right-click a table and choose the view/preview option to confirm rows come back.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Step 3 (route B, optional): the terminal route with psql

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    psql is the official PostgreSQL command-line client. It is the fastest way to run a saved .sql script against your database, and it is what you will see in most documentation. macOS does not ship it, so you install it. Skip this whole step if the GUI is working for you -- nothing later in the course requires it.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    📝
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    If you have never used Terminal

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Terminal is an app where you type one command, press Return, and read the text it prints back. Open it with Command + Space, type Terminal, press Return. Paste with Command + V like anywhere else. Commands below are one per line unless shown together -- press Return after each. Nothing here can damage your Mac, and you can close the window at any time.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    First check whether you already have psql. Run:

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    # psql --version: asks the command-line PostgreSQL client to print its version.
#   If it prints a number, psql is installed and on your PATH; if the shell
#   answers "command not found", the steps below install it.
psql --version

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    If that prints something like psql (PostgreSQL) 17.6, skip ahead to the connect command. If it prints zsh: command not found: psql, continue. Next, check for Homebrew, the package manager most Mac developers use to install command-line tools:

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    # brew --version: the same existence check, for Homebrew - the package manager
#   used to install psql on a Mac. An error here means Homebrew itself is missing.
brew --version

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    If that prints a version, skip to installing libpq. If it prints command not found, install Homebrew with the official one-line installer below. It will ask for your Mac login password (nothing appears on screen while you type it -- that is normal), it may first install Apple's Command Line Tools, which is a large download, and the whole thing can take five to fifteen minutes and print a lot of output.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    # The official Homebrew installer. Read it in pieces: curl downloads the install
#   script (-fsSL means fail quietly, stay silent, follow redirects), the $( )
#   hands that script's text to /bin/bash, and -c runs it. Only ever pipe a
#   script into a shell from a source you trust - this one is Homebrew's own.
/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)"

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    When it finishes, read the last few lines. Homebrew prints a Next steps: section containing two lines it wants you to run, and those lines already contain the correct path for your Mac. Copy them out of your own Terminal and run them. On an Apple Silicon Mac they look like this:

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    # echo ... >> ~/.zprofile: appends one line to your shell's startup file, so the
#   next terminal you open already knows where Homebrew lives. >> appends;
#   a single > would overwrite the file, which you do not want here.
echo 'eval "$(/opt/homebrew/bin/brew shellenv)"' >> ~/.zprofile

# eval: run that same line right now, so the CURRENT terminal is set up too
#   without you having to close and reopen it.
eval "$(/opt/homebrew/bin/brew shellenv)"
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    💡
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Intel Macs

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    On an Intel Mac, Homebrew installs to /usr/local instead of /opt/homebrew, so those two lines say /usr/local/bin/brew instead. This is why you copy the lines Homebrew printed for you rather than the ones printed here. Confirm it worked by running brew --version again -- it should now print a version number instead of command not found.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Now install the client. libpq is the PostgreSQL client package: it gives you psql without installing a database server on your Mac, which you do not need -- your server is Supabase.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    # brew install libpq: installs PostgreSQL's client library, which is what psql
#   is part of. It deliberately does not install a PostgreSQL server - your
#   database is on Supabase, and all you need locally is the client.
brew install libpq

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Homebrew installs libpq as keg-only, meaning it deliberately does not link it into your normal command folders (so it cannot collide with Apple's own copy or a full PostgreSQL install). PATH is the list of folders your shell searches for commands, so you add libpq's folder to it yourself. The line below appends one line to ~/.zshrc, your shell's configuration file, then reloads it. brew --prefix libpq works out the right folder on both Intel and Apple Silicon, so you do not have to know which Mac you own.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    # Add libpq's bin folder to PATH so the shell can find psql. brew --prefix libpq
#   prints where Homebrew put it, and the surrounding quotes make sure the path
#   survives even if it contains a space.
echo 'export PATH="'$(brew --prefix libpq)'/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.zshrc

# source: re-read the startup file so this terminal picks up the change now.
source ~/.zshrc

# The same check as before - this time it should print a version number.
psql --version

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    That last line is the proof: you should now see psql (PostgreSQL) 17.x or similar. If you still get command not found, close the Terminal window, open a new one, and try psql --version again.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    💡
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    If your shell is not zsh

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    macOS has used zsh by default since Catalina, so ~/.zshrc and ~/.zprofile are almost certainly right. Check with echo $SHELL. If it prints something ending in /bash, use ~/.bash_profile everywhere these instructions say ~/.zshrc or ~/.zprofile.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Now connect. Wrap the connection string in single quotes, and leave the password out of the command -- psql will prompt you for it, which keeps your password out of your shell history file. Replace the user and host with your own.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    # psql '<connection string>': opens an interactive session against the server.
#   Read the string in five parts - the postgresql:// scheme, the user before
#   the @, the host, the port after the colon, and the database name at the end.
#   The quotes are required, because the string contains characters the shell
#   would otherwise try to interpret.
psql 'postgresql://postgres.[PROJECT-REF]@aws-N-[REGION].pooler.supabase.com:5432/postgres'

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    psql prints Password for user postgres.[PROJECT-REF]:. Type or paste your password and press Return -- nothing appears on screen while you type, which is deliberate. A successful connection changes your prompt to postgres=> (some setups show postgres=#).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    ⚠️
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Single quotes, not double

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    If you do put the password inline, use single quotes: psql 'postgresql://...'. Double quotes still let zsh expand $, backticks, and backslashes inside the string, so a password containing $ would be silently mangled into something else and you would get an authentication failure you cannot explain. Single quotes protect everything except a single-quote character.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Prove you are talking to the right database. Run these two lines, pressing Return after each:

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    -- SELECT: two functions that describe the session rather than any table. They
--   answer "which database am I in, and who am I connected as?" - worth checking
--   before you run anything that changes data.
SELECT current_database(), current_user;

-- \dt: a psql meta-command, not SQL at all. Backslash commands are handled by
--   the client and never reach the server; this one lists your tables.
\dt

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    SELECT current_database(), current_user; is ordinary SQL and must end in a semicolon; it should report the database postgres. \dt is a psql meta-command (not SQL, no semicolon) that lists the tables in your search path -- that is the public schema -- so you should see your KimTay tables. If it prints Did not find any relations. you are connected to an empty project, not the one holding your course data. To run a script you have saved, quit and use the -f flag:

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    # psql ... -f file.sql: run a whole file of SQL and then exit, instead of opening
#   an interactive prompt. This is how a setup script is applied, and how you
#   re-run the same build over and over without retyping anything.
psql 'postgresql://postgres.[PROJECT-REF]@aws-N-[REGION].pooler.supabase.com:5432/postgres' -f ~/Desktop/my-queries.sql

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    When you are done, leave psql with \q, which returns you to the normal Terminal prompt:

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    -- \q: the psql meta-command that quits the session and returns you to the
--   shell. Ctrl-D does the same thing.
\q
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    📖
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Percent-encoding

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    A connection string is a URL, so the characters @, :, /, #, and ? already mean something structural in it. If your database password contains any of them and you paste it inline, the string is parsed wrongly and the connection fails. You can percent-encode them by hand (@ becomes %40, # becomes %23), but it is easier to let psql prompt you for the password as shown above, or to reset the password at Database then Settings to something using only letters and digits.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    📝
