                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    You are connecting as an owner, so RLS does not apply

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Both routes log you in as the postgres role, which owns your tables. In PostgreSQL a table's owner is not subject to that table's Row Level Security policies unless the table was explicitly set to FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY. So a query that returns rows here may return nothing through Supabase's API, where requests run as a restricted role. That is expected, not a bug. Worth knowing for later: tables you create with the Supabase Table Editor get RLS switched on for you, while tables you create by running CREATE TABLE in the SQL editor do not.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    When it does not work

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    The errors Mac students actually hit
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    What you seeWhyFix
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    zsh: command not found: psqlpsql is installed but not on your PATH, or libpq never installed.Re-run the echo ... >> ~/.zshrc and source ~/.zshrc lines, or just open a new Terminal window. Confirm the package is there with brew list libpq.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    FATAL: password authentication failed for user ...The password is wrong, or you left the literal [YOUR-PASSWORD] placeholder in the string, or a $ in your password was expanded by double quotes.Reset the password at Database then Settings, choosing letters and digits only. Copy the string again and replace the whole placeholder, brackets included -- or omit the password and let psql prompt you.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Tenant or user not foundThe user name lost its project reference. This message comes from the pooler, not from PostgreSQL.The user must read postgres. followed by your project reference, not plain postgres. Re-copy it from the Connect panel.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Connection timed out, or the client hangs with no message at allYou used the direct connection, which is IPv6-only on the free plan, and your network is IPv4.Go back to Connect and copy the Session pooler string instead. Confirm the host ends in pooler.supabase.com and the port is 5432.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    could not translate host name ... to address or nodename nor servname providedThe host name is wrong -- usually a typo, a truncated paste, or a host copied from a tutorial with the wrong aws-N prefix or region.Re-copy the host from your own Connect panel with the copy icon. Do not retype it by hand.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    server does not support SSL, but SSL was requiredRare against Supabase. It means the client is demanding a stricter SSL mode than it can verify -- for example verify-full with no root certificate loaded.Set SSL mode to require (pgAdmin: Parameters tab, +, SSL mode). prefer also works and is the default in both apps. Supabase does not force SSL by default, so plain prefer will connect and still encrypts.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • You copied the direct connection string when IPv6 works, or the Session pooler string on an IPv4-only network, from your own project's Connect panel.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • The user in your connection includes the dot and your project reference when the pooler requires it, and the password replaced the whole [YOUR-PASSWORD] placeholder, brackets and all.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • Either TablePlus or pgAdmin 4 connects and lists your KimTay tables under the public schema, or psql gives you a postgres=> prompt.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • SELECT current_database(), current_user; runs without error and reports the database postgres.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • \dt in psql, or the table list in your GUI, shows the KimTay tables -- not Did not find any relations.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • You saved the connection in your client, or saved the connection string in a file you can find, so you do not have to redo any of this next week.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • You know how to reset the database password at Database then Settings if you ever lose it.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    🔍 Check yourself: connecting from a Mac

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Pick an answer — the explanation opens right away.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Q1The command that isn't there

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    A student on a Mac follows the terminal route. brew install libpq finishes with no errors, but the very next command, psql --version, prints zsh: command not found: psql. They have not opened a new Terminal window since the install.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • ✘a. libpq is the PostgreSQL client package and does provide psql without any local database server, which you do not need since your server is Supabase.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • ✘b. This is a local tool problem, not a login problem: the shell never found a program to run, so no password was ever sent anywhere.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • ✔c. Correct - Homebrew installs libpq keg-only, so its folder must be added to PATH yourself, and a window opened before that edit will not see it.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • ✘d. The error names psql, not brew; if brew install succeeded then Homebrew is fine, and you can confirm the package with brew list libpq.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Remember: PATH is the list of folders your shell searches for commands, and a keg-only package is not in it until you add it and reload the shell.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Q2Three strings and only one right answer

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    A student opens the Connect panel and sees Direct connection, Transaction pooler, and Session pooler. They are on campus Wi-Fi and want to set up TablePlus on their Mac so they can browse the KimTay tables.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • ✔a. Correct - both pooler endpoints are reachable over IPv4 on every plan, and session mode behaves like a normal long-lived connection with prepared statements, which is what a desktop client wants.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • ✘b. On a free project the direct connection resolves to an IPv6 address only unless you buy the IPv4 add-on, so on a typical IPv4 network it just hangs and times out.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • ✘c. Transaction mode does not support prepared statements and is meant for serverless and edge functions, not for a desktop SQL client in this course.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • ✘d. Hosts differ by region and by the number after aws-, so copying a host from a tutorial is the single most common reason a connection never resolves.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Remember: For psql, TablePlus, or pgAdmin 4 on a laptop, always copy your own Session pooler string on port 5432.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Q3The failure that names the user

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    A student on a Mac pastes their connection string into psql in Terminal and gets FATAL: password authentication failed for user postgres.abcdefghijklmnopqrst. The client clearly reached a server, because the server is the thing complaining.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • ✘a. A wrong host shows up as could not translate host name ... to address, and no login is ever attempted because nothing was reached.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • ✘b. Losing the project reference produces the pooler's Tenant or user not found message; here the user was recognised, dot and reference included, and only the password was refused.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • ✘c. Row Level Security filters rows inside a session that already exists, and the owner is exempt anyway unless the table was set to FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • ✔d. Correct - those are exactly the three causes the Mac troubleshooting table lists; replace the whole placeholder brackets included, or leave the password out and let psql prompt you.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Remember: Read the error literally: an authentication failure means you reached the right server with the wrong secret, so fix the password, not the host.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    S-5 Connect from your own machine: Windows

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    By the end of this section you will have your Supabase database open on your own Windows machine in two different ways: in pgAdmin 4, a point-and-click tool with a tree of tables you can browse, and in psql, the command-line client, run from PowerShell. Both talk to the same database you created in the browser, so a table you build here shows up in the Supabase Table Editor a second later. You do not need a local PostgreSQL server for any of this. You only need the client tools and your connection string.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    📝
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Before you start

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    You need three things: a Supabase project you already created, the database password you chose when you created it, and a Windows 10 or Windows 11 machine where you are allowed to install software. Budget about 20 minutes. On a school lab machine without administrator rights you can still install pgAdmin 4 for the current user, and you can still edit your own User variables Path, but you cannot edit System variables -- the steps below say where that matters. If you cannot install anything at all, everything in this section can also be done in the Supabase SQL Editor in the browser.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Step 1: copy your connection string

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Every tool below asks for the same five facts: host, port, database name, user, and password. Supabase hands you all five in one line of text called a connection string. It lives behind the Connect button at the top of your project dashboard. Older tutorials send you digging through Project Settings; the Connect button is the current path and it is faster.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    1

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Open your project

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Go to supabase.com/dashboard and click your project. Free projects are paused after about a week with no database activity. If yours says Paused, click Restore project and wait for the dashboard to finish loading before continuing. You will know it worked when the project overview page shows charts instead of a paused banner.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    2

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Click Connect

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    The Connect button sits at the top of the dashboard, near the project name. A panel opens listing several connection strings, each with its own tab or heading.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    3

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Choose the session-mode pooler on port 5432

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Pick the string labelled Session pooler. Some dashboards now label this group Shared pooler with a Session mode choice -- it is the same thing. Whatever the label, the string you want has pooler.supabase.com in the host and ends with :5432/postgres. Do not take the :6543 string: that is transaction mode, which drops session features such as prepared statements and will make ordinary tools behave strangely. Do not take Direct connection either: that host (db.<ref>.supabase.co) resolves only to an IPv6 address unless the project has the paid IPv4 add-on, and most home and campus networks in the United States are still IPv4-only, so it looks like it hangs and then times out. The shared pooler answers on IPv4 on every plan, including Free.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    4

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Copy it and paste your password in

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    The copied string contains the placeholder [YOUR-PASSWORD], brackets included. Replace that whole placeholder, brackets and all, with the database password you chose when you created the project. Nothing else in the string changes.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    5

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Park it somewhere safe for the next twenty minutes

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Paste it into Notepad while you work through this section. Do not paste it into a shared document, a Discord channel, or a GitHub repository -- it is the key to your database.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    postgresql://postgres.abcdefghijklmnopqrst:MyDbPassw0rd@aws-1-us-east-1.pooler.supabase.com:5432/postgres

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    That is an example, not your string. Copy yours from the Connect panel and never retype this one: the host prefix is aws-0 on some projects and aws-1 on others, and the region part changes with where your project lives. The panel may also start the string with postgres:// instead of postgresql://; both are accepted, so leave whichever you were given.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Read your line left to right and you have every field the tools ask for: the user is postgres.abcdefghijklmnopqrst (the word postgres, a dot, then your project reference), the password comes after the colon, the host is everything between @ and the last colon, the port is 5432, and the database name after the final slash is postgres.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    ⚠️
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    If your password contains punctuation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    A connection string is a URL, so a few characters cannot appear in the password as-is: @, :, /, ?, #, [, ] and %. If your password contains any of them, replace each one with its percent code inside the string -- @ becomes %40, # becomes %23, ? becomes %3F, / becomes %2F, : becomes %3A, % becomes %25. So p@ss#1 is written p%40ss%231. Supabase does not do this escaping for you when it builds the string, which is why a correct password can still produce a confusing failure. The -h -p -d -U flag form shown later avoids the problem entirely, because there the password is typed at a prompt rather than embedded in a URL.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    ⚠️
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Lost the password

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    The database password is shown once, when the project is created. Supabase cannot show it to you again. If you do not have it, set a new one from the dashboard: Database in the left sidebar, then Settings (the page whose address ends in /database/settings), then Reset database password. In older dashboards the same page is Project Settings then Database. Resetting briefly restarts the database and breaks every tool you already saved the old password in, so update pgAdmin afterwards and copy a fresh connection string.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Step 2: connect with pgAdmin 4

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    pgAdmin 4 is the free, official graphical client for PostgreSQL. If you install PostgreSQL from the EDB installer described in step 3, pgAdmin 4 comes bundled with it and there is nothing else to download. If you would rather not install a server at all, download pgAdmin 4 on its own from pgadmin.org/download/pgadmin-4-windows/ -- the current release is version 9.x, the installer is digitally signed, and it supports Windows 10 and later. Either way, launch it from the Start menu by typing pgAdmin. The first launch takes a few seconds and opens in a window that looks like a web page; that is normal.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    1

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Set a master password if you are asked for one

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Some installs ask you to create a master password on first launch. This is a local password that protects the saved server passwords on this computer; it is not your Supabase password. Since version 7.2, pgAdmin uses the Windows credential store when it can and may never ask, so do not go looking for the prompt if it does not appear. If you do get it, pick something you will remember and write it down.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    2

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Register the server

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    In the left panel (the Object Explorer), right-click Servers and choose Register then Server.... In some builds this reads Create then Server.... A dialog opens with tabs across the top: General, Connection, Parameters, and a few more.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    3

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    General tab

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    In Name, type something you will recognise, for example Supabase KimTay. This name is only a label for you and has no effect on the connection.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    4

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Connection tab

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Fill in Host name/address, Port, Maintenance database, Username, and Password from your connection string, using the table below. Type the password in plainly here -- do not percent-encode it in pgAdmin, because this is not a URL. Tick Save password? so you are not retyping it every session.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    5

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Parameters tab

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Click + to add a parameter, choose SSL mode, and set it to require. pgAdmin's default is prefer, which already encrypts the connection to Supabase, so this is a belt-and-braces step rather than a requirement; require makes it an error rather than a silent fallback if encryption is ever unavailable. In older builds this setting sits on a tab named SSL instead.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    6

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Save and check

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Click Save. You will know it worked when the server appears in the tree with a coloured (not greyed-out) icon and no error dialog. Expand Supabase KimTay then Databases then postgres then Schemas then public then Tables to see the tables you have created. If you have not created any yet, Tables expands to nothing -- that is expected, not a failure.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    pgAdmin 4 Connection tab, filled in from the connection string
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    pgAdmin fieldWhat to enterExample
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Host name/addressEverything between @ and the last :aws-1-us-east-1.pooler.supabase.com
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    PortThe number after the last : and before the final slash5432
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Maintenance databaseThe word after the final slashpostgres
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Usernamepostgres dot your project reference (everything between // and the first :)postgres.abcdefghijklmnopqrst
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    PasswordYour database password, typed literally (no percent codes here)MyDbPassw0rd
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    💡
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Running SQL in pgAdmin

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    With your database selected in the tree, open Tools then Query Tool. That gives you an editor exactly like the Supabase SQL Editor. Paste your CREATE TABLE REP ... statement and press F5 to run it; the Data Output panel at the bottom reports how long it took, and Messages shows CREATE TABLE when it succeeded. Tools also has a PSQL Tool, which is a real psql session embedded in pgAdmin -- a useful fallback if step 3 gives you trouble, since it needs no PATH setup.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    TablePlus is a popular alternative with a cleaner interface, and it runs on Windows. It is paid software with a trial that has no published expiry date, but the trial limits you to two open tabs and two open windows at a time, and advanced filters are not available in the free version on Windows at all. Licences start at $99 one time for a single device. For this course pgAdmin 4 does everything you need at no cost, so treat TablePlus as optional.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Step 3: get psql and run it from PowerShell

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    psql is the text client that ships with PostgreSQL. It is worth learning because every server, every tutorial, and every job posting assumes it. On Windows the usual way to get it is the EDB installer that postgresql.org links to, and you can install the client tools without installing a database server on your laptop.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    1

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Download the installer

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Go to enterprisedb.com/downloads/postgres-postgresql-downloads and download the Windows x86-64 installer for the newest version listed (18.4 at the time of writing). This is the download that postgresql.org/download/windows/ links to. There is no 32-bit build any more.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    2

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Run it and reach Select Components

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Right-click the downloaded file and choose Run as administrator if you have that right; otherwise just run it. Accept the default install directory. On the Select Components screen you will see four checkboxes: PostgreSQL Server, pgAdmin 4, Stack Builder, and Command Line Tools.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    3

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Choose what to install

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Command Line Tools is the component that provides psql -- leave it checked. Leave pgAdmin 4 checked so you get the graphical client from step 2 for free. You can uncheck PostgreSQL Server and Stack Builder, because your database lives at Supabase, not on your laptop. If you do leave the server checked, the installer will ask you to set a local superuser password and a port; that password has nothing to do with Supabase, and you can ignore the local server afterwards.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    4

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Note the install folder

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    The tools land in C:\Program Files\PostgreSQL\18\bin, where 18 is the major version you installed -- open C:\Program Files\PostgreSQL in File Explorer and use whatever number you actually see there. Go into bin and confirm psql.exe is present. Leave the File Explorer address bar showing that full path; you are about to copy it.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    5

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Add that folder to PATH

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    The installer does not put this folder on the system path, so Windows does not yet know where psql.exe is. Press the Windows key, type environment, and open Edit the system environment variables. In System Properties click Environment Variables.... If you have administrator rights, select Path under System variables; if you do not, select Path under User variables for <your name> instead -- either works for your own account. Click Edit, click New, paste C:\Program Files\PostgreSQL\18\bin (with your version number), then click OK on all three dialogs. There must be no quotation marks and no trailing backslash.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    6

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Open a fresh PowerShell and verify

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Close every PowerShell and Command Prompt window you already had open -- they captured the old PATH and will not see the change. Open a new one from the Start menu (type powershell) and run the two checks below.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    # where.exe psql: the Windows equivalent of asking "is psql installed, and
#   where?". It prints the full path if the shell can find it and says nothing
#   useful if it cannot.
where.exe psql

# And the version check, which confirms the program actually runs.
psql --version

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    where.exe psql should print the full path to psql.exe; it is how you prove the PATH edit took effect. Use where.exe, with the extension, because a bare where in PowerShell means something else entirely. Then psql --version should print a line like psql (PostgreSQL) 18.4. If the version printed is older than the one you installed, some other copy of psql is earlier in your PATH -- the path from where.exe tells you which.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Now connect. Wrap the connection string in single quotation marks. Unquoted, PowerShell treats several characters that can appear in a password as punctuation of its own: & is reserved and produces The ampersand (&) character is not allowed, ; ends the command, # starts a comment, and a space splits the argument in two. Single quotes rather than double quotes matter, because inside double quotes PowerShell expands anything starting with $, so a password containing $ would silently arrive wrong. If your password itself contains a single quote, double it ('') inside the quoted string.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    # The same connect command on Windows, with a real-looking connection string.
#   Everything before the @ is the account, everything after it is the address of
#   the server. Never paste a string with a live password into a chat, a
#   screenshot or a commit.
psql 'postgresql://postgres.abcdefghijklmnopqrst:MyDbPassw0rd@aws-1-us-east-1.pooler.supabase.com:5432/postgres'

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    When it connects, PowerShell prints a psql banner and the prompt changes to postgres=>. That prompt is how you know you are in. From there you are typing SQL, and every statement ends with a semicolon -- until you type the semicolon and press Enter, psql keeps waiting and shows a postgres-> continuation prompt instead. A few commands start with a backslash; those are psql's own shortcuts, not SQL, and they do not take a semicolon.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    -- \dt: list the tables you have created.
\dt

-- An ordinary SQL query, typed at the same prompt. psql passes anything that is
--   not a backslash command straight to the server.
SELECT REP_NUM, LAST_NAME, FIRST_NAME FROM REP;

-- \d TABLE: describe one table - its columns, types and keys. This is the
--   quickest way to check a table matches what you meant to build.
\d CUSTOMER

-- \q: quit.
\q

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    \dt lists your tables, \d CUSTOMER describes one table the way DESCRIBE does in MySQL, and \q quits back to PowerShell. Two things will surprise you. First, \dt prints your table names in lower case (rep, customer) even though you created them in capitals: PostgreSQL folds unquoted identifiers to lower case, and psql folds the name in \d CUSTOMER the same way, which is why the capitalised version still matches. Second, \dt and the SELECT only work once the tables exist -- if you have not run your CREATE TABLE statements yet, run them first, here or in the Supabase SQL Editor.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    💡
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Keep your password out of your history

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    PowerShell records every command you type in %APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\PowerShell\PSReadLine\ConsoleHost_history.txt, so the line above leaves your password in a plain text file that survives reboots. On a lab or shared machine, pass the pieces as flags instead and let psql prompt you: psql -h aws-1-us-east-1.pooler.supabase.com -p 5432 -d postgres -U postgres.abcdefghijklmnopqrst. This form also sidesteps percent-encoding, since the password is never part of a URL. Nothing appears on screen while you type the password, not even dots. That is normal -- type it and press Enter.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    💡
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    If you would rather not touch PATH

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    You can run psql by its full path without editing any environment variable. In PowerShell a quoted path has to be launched with the call operator &: & 'C:\Program Files\PostgreSQL\18\bin\psql.exe' 'postgresql://...'. The PSQL Tool inside pgAdmin (Tools then PSQL Tool) is another PATH-free way to get the same prompt.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    When it does not work

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Windows connection problems and what to do about them
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    What you seeWhat it meansWhat to do
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    'psql' is not recognized as the name of a cmdletWindows cannot find psql.exeThe PATH entry is missing, mistyped, or the window is stale. Run where.exe psql -- if it prints nothing, re-check the Path entry (no quotes, no trailing backslash, correct version number), then close every PowerShell window and open a new one.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    psql: error: connection to server ... FATAL: Tenant or user not foundThe pooler did not recognise the user nameOn the pooler the user must be postgres. plus your project reference, not plain postgres. Re-copy the whole string from the Connect panel rather than editing the old one by hand.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    The password prompt repeats, or password authentication failed for userWrong password, or punctuation in the password broke the URLRe-check the password. If it contains @ : / ? # [ ] %, percent-encode those characters inside the connection string, or switch to the -h -p -d -U flag form and type the password at the prompt. If the password is genuinely lost, reset it at Database then Settings and copy a fresh string.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    The ampersand (&) character is not allowedPowerShell is reading part of your connection string as a commandWrap the whole string in single quotation marks, or use the -h -p -d -U flag form instead.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    You connect but the password is rejected only in PowerShell, never in pgAdminYour password contains $ and you used double quotesPowerShell expanded it as a variable. Use single quotes.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    could not connect to server: Connection timed out after a long waitYou are on the direct connection (db. host) and your network is IPv4-only, or a firewall blocks outbound port 5432Use the session-mode pooler string with the pooler.supabase.com host. If that still times out, test on a phone hotspot to confirm the school network is the blocker, and use the Supabase SQL Editor in the browser meanwhile.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    pgAdmin: could not translate host name ... to addressA typo in the host, or the square brackets were left inRetype the host from the Connect panel. There should be no [ or ] anywhere in any field, and the prefix is aws-0 or aws-1 depending on the project -- do not copy the example from this page.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    An SSL or certificate error in pgAdminThe SSL mode parameter is set to something stricter than your setup supportsSet SSL mode to require on the Parameters tab. verify-full additionally needs the Supabase CA certificate downloaded from Database then Settings; you do not need it for this course.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    You connect, but \dt says Did not find any relationsYou are connected to an empty schemaThat is expected until you run your CREATE TABLE statements. Run them here or in the Supabase SQL Editor, then try \dt again. Remember the names come back in lower case.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    📝
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Windows Defender Firewall

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Windows may pop up a firewall prompt the first time pgAdmin or psql runs. These tools make outbound connections only, so you can decline the prompt asking to allow incoming connections and everything will still work. If your school network blocks outbound port 5432 entirely, no local setting will fix that -- use the browser SQL Editor on campus and your own network at home.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    ⚠️
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Tables you create here are not protected by Row Level Security

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Supabase turns on Row Level Security automatically for tables made in the Table Editor, but not for tables created with SQL -- which is what you are doing in psql and in the Query Tool. Your new table will show up in the Table Editor flagged as unrestricted, meaning anyone holding your project's public API key could read it. That is acceptable for coursework data, but get in the habit now: run ALTER TABLE REP ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; on any table holding data you would not publish.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • where.exe psql prints a path ending in \bin\psql.exe in a newly opened PowerShell window.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • psql --version prints a version number that matches the version you installed.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • psql '<your connection string>' reaches the postgres=> prompt.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • \dt lists the tables you have created so far, in lower case, or reports none if you have not created any yet.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • pgAdmin 4 shows your server in the left tree with no error, and expands down to Schemas then public then Tables.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • A table you create in psql appears in the Supabase Table Editor in the browser after a refresh.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • Your password is stored somewhere private, not in a shared file, a repository, or a screenshot.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    🔍 Check yourself: connecting from Windows
