                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                ⚠️
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                The one deadline that matters

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Get your scope paragraph approved in session 1 or 2. Everything after it depends on that decision, and a scope that is too large is the single most common reason a project like this stalls. If your instructor asks you to cut two entities, cut them — a small database designed well scores far better than a large one left half-built.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Setup Getting Students a Real Database to Build OnObjective 4 Objective 6

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                With the VPS out of the picture, there are two solid paths, and they pair well together: a hosted database (Supabase) for the moment your students want something genuinely reachable beyond their own laptop, and a real local install on their own Mac or Windows machine for everyday coursework.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Path 1: Supabase — a hosted database, no server for anyone to manage

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                💡
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                You already have a Supabase account connected

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Supabase (which shows up as already connected in your account) is managed PostgreSQL with a generous free tier, a browser-based SQL editor, and zero servers for you to patch or back up. It's Postgres rather than MySQL, which is actually a natural, low-stakes place to reinforce Lesson 3-2's cross-engine comparison — students will notice a few syntax differences first-hand.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Two ways to structure it for a class:

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                ModelHow it worksBest for
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Students self-serveEach student creates their own free account at supabase.com and their own project; they submit a link/credentials or screenshots for grading.Zero setup on your end, at the cost of losing central oversight.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                You provision per studentUsing your existing Supabase organization, create one project per student (or per small group) yourself.Central control — you can reset, inspect, or revoke any project directly.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                📖
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Where this fits the capstone

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Supabase is the natural home for the capstone project's "deploy it somewhere real" step (see the previous section) — it's the one option here that's actually reachable outside a student's own laptop, which is what makes the finished project feel like more than a classroom exercise.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Path 2: Install a real DBMS locally (Mac and Windows)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                For day-to-day Module 1–3 practice, a local install means no accounts, no internet dependency, and (if you pick MySQL) an exact syntax match to what this site's sandbox and Module 3 teach:

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Windows

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Download MySQL Installer for Windows from dev.mysql.com/downloads/installer. Run it, choose the "Developer Default" (or "Custom") setup type, and make sure MySQL Server and MySQL Workbench are both selected. Step through the configuration wizard, set a root password, and keep the default port (3306). Workbench opens at the end and connects straight to your new local server.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Mac

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Easiest path: download the macOS installer (.dmg) from dev.mysql.com/downloads/mysql, run it (note the temporary root password it shows you during setup), then separately download MySQL Workbench from dev.mysql.com/downloads/workbench and drag it into Applications. If you're comfortable with Homebrew instead: brew install mysql && brew services start mysql, then brew install --cask mysqlworkbench for the GUI.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                MySQL Workbench is the closest match to everything Module 3 teaches — same CREATE DATABASE, same data types, same DESCRIBE syntax.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Windows

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Download the installer from postgresql.org/download/windows (the EDB installer). Run it, keep PostgreSQL Server and pgAdmin 4 selected, set a password for the postgres superuser, and keep the default port (5432). You can skip Stack Builder at the end. pgAdmin 4 is your GUI going forward.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Mac

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Simplest option: Postgres.app (postgresapp.com) — drag it into Applications, double-click to initialize a server, and it's running. Add its command-line tools to your PATH from the app's own instructions if you want to use psql from Terminal. Homebrew alternative: brew install postgresql@16 && brew services start postgresql@16. Either way, download pgAdmin 4 separately for a graphical client.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Worth it if you'd rather standardize on Postgres end-to-end — nothing changes in syntax between local practice and the Supabase deployment step below.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                XAMPP

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                apachefriends.org — one installer for Windows, Mac, or Linux. Bundles Apache, MySQL/MariaDB, and phpMyAdmin (a browser-based SQL tool). Start the "MySQL" module from the XAMPP control panel, then open localhost/phpmyadmin in a browser and run SQL directly — no separate desktop client to install.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                MAMP

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                mamp.info — the Mac-originated equivalent (also available for Windows), bundling MySQL and phpMyAdmin the same way. Same pitch: one download, one control panel, SQL through a browser tab.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                The gentlest on-ramp for less technical students — a single installer and a web page, instead of a separate server plus a separate desktop GUI to configure.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Comparing the options

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                💡
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                A simple way to combine both

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Have students install MySQL (or the XAMPP/MAMP bundle) locally for Modules 1–3 and the early parts of the capstone — no accounts, no internet dependency, closest match to what this site teaches. Then for the capstone's deployment step, everyone moves their finished schema to their own free Supabase project. If you'd rather remove local installs entirely and avoid supporting 20–30 different laptops, Supabase alone (used from Lesson 3-1 onward) also works fine — you'd just note for students that its SQL is Postgres, not MySQL.
